Its product line includes the 5,000 lbf Hadley oxygen-rich staged-combustion liquid engine — the first Ursa Major engine to reach flight qualification for hypersonic missions — and Draper, a storable, throttleable, restartable engine for tactical hypersonic strike, missile defense and rapid in-space maneuver, alongside a solid rocket motor line validated through static fire and a chemical propulsion capability for tactical satellite bus systems. Ursa Major was the first American company to successfully fire an oxygen-rich staged combustion engine; it states it has delivered more than 100 engines and logged over 100,000 seconds of hotfire testing, with engines and motors more than 80 percent 3D printed by mass. The company is AS9100D, ISO 9001 and CMMC Level 2 certified. Ursa Major is a hardware manufacturer selling to government and prime-contractor customers: it publishes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, developer portal or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Continuum
providers.description: Continuum (gocontinuum.ai) is an AI-powered platform that automates B2B returns, warranties, and repairs for distributors and manufacturers. It handles the post-sales workflow end to end through four solution hubs: a Customer Hub with self-service warranty and return portals, a Warehouse Hub for one-click receiving, inspection and dispute processing, a Vendor & Finance Hub for automated vendor engagement and accounts-receivable management, and a Manufacturer Warranty Hub for warranty claim automation. The company reports outcomes such as a 70% reduction in returns labor cost, a 30% increase in profitability, and an 8% reduction in customer churn. Continuum integrates with major distribution ERP systems (Infor, NetSuite, Epicor, Oracle, Acumatica). Based in Chicago, it is seed-funded and backed by Cowboy Ventures. Continuum is SOC 2 audited and publishes a public trust center. No public developer API or documentation is available at this time.

providers.name: Diagon
providers.description: Diagon is a California-based industrial equipment sourcing company building Albus, an equipment intelligence platform for manufacturing buyers and sellers. Buyers search across millions of industrial equipment listings, compare models, specifications, pricing and availability, and connect directly with sellers; sellers publish AI-powered catalogs, reach qualified buyer demand, and see live equipment searches in real time. Diagon indexes manufacturing equipment products, suppliers and service providers, bringing hardware, services and financing into a consolidated procurement experience. Founded by a team out of Tesla, Bright Machines, Rivian and Snackpass, and backed by Anthemis under its data, tech and infrastructure thesis. Diagon publishes no public developer API today; its /api surface is an authenticated first-party application API (Clerk-based session auth) and is disallowed in robots.txt.

providers.name: Gecko Robotics
providers.description: Gecko Robotics is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania based AI and robotics company that inspects and manages critical physical infrastructure. Its wall-climbing, aerial and submersible robots capture full-coverage ultrasonic, visual and other sensor readings from boilers, pressure vessels, tanks, pipelines, ship hulls and decks, which are fused with facility records and operational data inside Cantilever, the company's AI-powered operating platform for the built world. Cantilever quantifies corrosion rates, predicts remaining asset life and prioritizes capital and maintenance decisions for customers across defense, power, oil and gas, steel, pulp and paper, mining and advanced manufacturing. Cantilever is delivered as a closed, authenticated enterprise SaaS at cantilever.app; Gecko Robotics publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or self-serve API program, and integrations are arranged through the company directly.

providers.name: Poka
providers.description: Poka is a manufacturing-focused connected worker platform that helps industrial and frontline teams standardize work execution across learning, daily management, and operations. It combines digital work instructions, on-the-job training, skills management, and factory-floor knowledge sharing with embedded Industrial AI. Poka exposes a RESTful Poka API for building integrations with third-party systems (MES, CMMS, LMS, QMS, ERP, BI), SCIM for automated user provisioning from identity providers, the Poka Automate iPaaS, and a Poka Data Lake for BI/reporting. Poka is part of IFS and runs regionally in the US, Canada, and EU.

providers.name: Tacto
providers.description: Tacto (Tacto Technology GmbH) is a Munich-based AI procurement intelligence platform for manufacturing companies. It unifies internal ERP and engineering data with external market intelligence to power AI agents that automate procurement work across four areas: Supplier Intelligence (centralized supplier management with documents, evaluations and performance data), Spend & Cost Intelligence (spend analysis and savings identification), Sourcing Intelligence (AI-optimized RFQ and price inquiries) and Compliance Intelligence (automated regulatory and supply-chain due-diligence detection). Tacto is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified and GDPR compliant with EU-only hosting and an audit log of every AI action. It does not publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures the company's corporate, security and compliance surface.

providers.name: Vanderhall Motor Works
providers.description: Vanderhall Motor Works is a privately held American vehicle manufacturer founded in 2010 by Steve Hall and headquartered in Provo, Utah. The company hand-builds three-wheeled autocycles — the Laguna, Venice, Venice Speedster, Carmel and Santarosa — alongside the all-electric Edison and the quad-motor Brawley off-road UTV, selling through an independent dealer network rather than direct to consumers. Its software footprint is internal rather than commercial: Vanderhall runs a dealer portal, an admin portal and a parts/accessory shop on its own domain, and the admin portal publishes an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint at https://portal.vanderhallusa.com/mcp with RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata and RFC 7591 dynamic client registration. There is no public developer program, no published OpenAPI, and no public API reference.

providers.name: Archer Aviation
providers.description: Archer Aviation is a U.S. eVTOL aircraft company developing Midnight, a piloted four-passenger all-electric aircraft designed for rapid back-to-back urban flights of roughly 20-50 miles with a ~10 minute charge between trips. Archer is pursuing FAA Type Certification and operates through commercial and defense business lines. Key partnerships include Stellantis (contract manufacturing at Archer's Covington, Georgia facility), United Airlines (launch routes including the Manhattan-Newark corridor), and a Launch Edition program in the United Arab Emirates with Abu Dhabi Aviation. Archer also has a dedicated defense division (Archer Defense) developing hybrid VTOL platforms with Anduril and supporting U.S. government missions. The company trades on the NYSE under ACHR.

providers.name: Intenseye
providers.description: Intenseye is an AI-powered workplace safety platform that applies computer vision to a facility's existing CCTV cameras to detect unsafe conditions and behaviors in real time and prevent Serious Injuries and Fatalities (SIF). Its Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) product surfaces hazards, compliance gaps, and operational risks across manufacturing, logistics, food & beverage, and other high-risk industries, and can trigger Hard Stop emergency alerts. Intenseye offers cloud, private cloud, and on-premise deployment, is SOC 2 / AICPA certified and GDPR-aligned, uses AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS in transit, and does not use facial recognition. Backed by Insight Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Point Nine. Intenseye publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal; product access is through its dashboard and login. It maintains a public GitHub organization of mostly open-source forks and workshops rather than first-party client libraries.

providers.name: Retrocausal
providers.description: Retrocausal builds AI-powered copilot software for manufacturing operations, applying patented computer vision and machine learning to manual assembly lines. Its products include Assembly Copilot (real-time AI-tracked work instructions, poka-yoke error prevention, and cycle-level video traceability), Kaizen Copilot (AI-powered time studies, standard work, automatic line balancing, and ergonomic analysis for industrial engineers), and Ergo Copilot (ergonomic risk assessment from smartphone video). The platform runs on AWS, is ISO 27001 certified, and integrates with MES systems, OPC UA for PLCs and smart tools, barcode scanners, torque wrenches, light towers, and projectors, with SSO via Azure Active Directory and Okta. Retrocausal is a Techstars portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API; integrations are delivered as custom MES/OPC UA and identity connections rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: TE Connectivity
providers.description: TE Connectivity is a global manufacturer of connectors and sensors headquartered in Galway, Ireland with operational headquarters in Berwyn, Pennsylvania. TE provides electrical connectivity and sensor solutions for transportation, industrial, and communications markets, with strong automotive Tier 1 supply relationships.

providers.name: BWX Technologies
providers.description: BWX Technologies is a manufacturer of nuclear components and provider of nuclear services to the U.S. government and commercial customers worldwide. The company delivers innovative nuclear solutions across naval propulsion, small modular reactors, nuclear fuel, medical isotopes, and complex site operations.

providers.name: CADDi
providers.description: CADDi is a Tokyo-headquartered manufacturing-technology company that builds an AI Data Platform for industrial manufacturers. Its two products, CADDi Drawer and CADDi Quote, aggregate scattered 2D engineering drawings and supply-chain data into a single searchable asset, offering keyword and drawing-similarity search, automatic extraction of dimensions, text and shapes, and AI-assisted quotation and sourcing. The platform serves procurement, engineering, sales, production, quality, and leadership teams across automotive, robotics, and precision-machinery sectors, and connects to ERP, CAM, CAD, and quality systems via batch and CSV imports. CADDi was surfaced as a portfolio company of Atomico and DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK.

providers.name: Hithium
providers.description: HiTHIUM (Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese energy storage company founded in 2019 that designs and manufactures lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, modules and complete battery energy storage systems (BESS) for utility-scale, commercial and industrial, and residential applications. The product line runs from large-format prismatic ESS cells through liquid-cooled multi-megawatt-hour container systems to the HeroEE residential and portable range marketed at hero-ee.com. Company material reports roughly 8,000 staff, more than 1,100 R&D engineers and over 3,900 patents. Product pages publish named certifications including UL 1973, UL 9540, UL 9540A, NFPA 855, IEC 62619, IEC 62477, IEC 63056, IEC 61000 and UN 38.3. HiTHIUM operates a Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) running an IEC 62443-aligned vulnerability management process, and publishes numbered cybersecurity bulletins with CVE references and remediation guidance at hithium.com/support/security.html. HiTHIUM publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or Postman contract, no SDKs, no CLI, no webhook catalog and no MCP or A2A agent surface; third-party integration happens over Modbus/CAN interfaces described in datasheets and manuals that sit behind the download-center account gate, and the HeroEE consumer app's backend is undocumented.

providers.name: LightSource
providers.description: LightSource is an AI-native direct materials procurement platform that connects engineering, procurement, and suppliers across the full sourcing lifecycle from concept to award. The product automates RFX creation and distribution, AI-assisted bid analysis, supplier collaboration and quote normalization across custom quote formats, and ongoing cost tracking, with more than 20,000 suppliers live on the network. It is sold to procurement and supply-chain teams in automotive, electronics, chemicals, medical devices, construction, and forest products, and the company reports sourcing cost reductions of 3-25% for customers including Time Manufacturing (Versalift), Arxada, BRP, and Canada Goose. LightSource is SOC 2 Type 2 attested and supports SSO and role-based access control. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; its docs host is an end-user and supplier help center.

providers.name: Phaidra
providers.description: Phaidra builds AI agents for autonomous data center and industrial operations, using reinforcement learning to control cooling, power, and workloads in mission-critical facilities. Its products include Phaidra Prism, an LLM for data center operations that helps technicians identify, prioritize, and resolve infrastructure issues, and Phaidra Factory, self-learning AI agents that continuously monitor and optimize thermal reliability, energy efficiency, and IT capacity to maximize tokens per watt across AI factories. Phaidra is an enterprise vendor with no public API or developer program; this profile captures its public security, compliance, and web posture. Backed by Index Ventures.

providers.name: Rondo Energy
providers.description: Rondo Energy is an Alameda, California industrial decarbonization company led by CEO John O'Donnell that builds the Rondo Heat Battery (RHB), a thermal energy storage system that converts intermittent wind and solar electricity into heat stored in thousands of tons of refractory brick at temperatures up to 1,500C and returns it as continuous steam, thermal oil, superheated air, or combined heat and power at rated outputs from 2MWth to over 100MWth. The RHB is sold as a drop-in replacement for a fossil-fuel boiler, via capital purchase, lease, or heat purchase agreement, into cement, food and beverage, chemicals, fuels and ethanol, textiles, pulp and paper, mining, pharmaceuticals, and direct air capture. Rondo operates the world's largest industrial heat battery and has announced a 90GWh factory plan with Siam Cement Group, backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Catalyst, Energy Impact Partners, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Rio Tinto, SABIC, Aramco Ventures, and the European Investment Bank. Rondo sells hardware and delivered heat, not software: it publishes no developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Avatr Technology
providers.description: AVATR Technology (Chongqing) Co., Ltd. (阿维塔科技) is a Chinese premium intelligent electric-vehicle manufacturer headquartered in Chongqing, founded in 2018 as a joint venture in which Changan Automobile and CATL are the two largest shareholders and Huawei supplies the smart-cockpit and advanced driver-assistance stack. Its vehicles — the AVATR 11 and 12, the volume 06 and 07 (battery-electric and range-extended), and the limited 011 and 012 — are built on the jointly developed CHN smart-EV platform, a six-layer architecture spanning the mechanical, energy, electronic/electrical architecture, vehicle operating system, vehicle function application and cloud big-data layers. AVATR produced 73,606 vehicles in 2024 and sells through mainland China plus overseas markets including Hong Kong, Singapore, Thailand, Sri Lanka, the UAE and Qatar, with design and engineering offices in Shanghai and Munich. AVATR is a vehicle manufacturer, not a software vendor: www.avatr.com is a marketing and configurator site with no developer portal, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable specification. The only live agent surface anywhere on an AVATR hostname is platform-provided — the official Hong Kong site runs on Wix and exposes the Wix Site MCP endpoint plus a Wix-generated llms.txt over its public marketing content.

providers.name: Active Membranes
providers.description: Active Membranes is a California water-technology company, founded in 2022 out of research at the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering, that builds electrically conductive "electro-active" reverse-osmosis membranes for desalination and water reuse. Where a conventional RO membrane filters passively and is cleaned after it fouls, Active Membranes embeds conductive material in the membrane's polymer matrix and uses a control unit it calls the Active Box to apply a tunable low electrical potential at the membrane surface, electrostatically repelling scale-forming ions and charged organic foulants in real time. The modules ship in the standard 8-inch by 40-inch spiral-wound format so they retrofit into existing pressure vessels, and are aimed at seawater and brackish desalination, produced-water and industrial reuse. The company reports field results including roughly 48% less irreversible fouling in produced-water reuse, up to 70% longer cleaning cycles in brackish water, and a Ventura County study citing about 57% lower cost and 64% less footprint. It has raised roughly $3.24M in seed funding from Natural Ventures, Echo River Capital and Pacifica Water Solutions, won the 2023 Global Water Summit Water Technology Idol award, and was selected as a Qualified Team in the XPRIZE Water Scarcity competition. Active Membranes sells capital equipment, not software: it operates no developer program, publishes no OpenAPI, GraphQL or SDK, and lists no pricing. It does, however, serve two machine-readable surfaces from its own hostname — a substantial hand-written /llms.txt, and a live, unauthenticated Model Context Protocol endpoint at /_api/mcp exposing nine tools over the public site content. Both are Wix platform features the company chose to enable and advertise rather than first-party engineering.

providers.name: Phononic
providers.description: Phononic is a Durham, North Carolina solid-state cooling company founded by CEO Tony Atti that replaces compressor-based refrigeration with semiconductor thermoelectric devices. Its products cool optical and fiber transceivers, co-packaged optics, GPU high-bandwidth memory, LiDAR sensors, medical and vaccine cold chain, grocery retail merchandising and HVAC. The current focus is AI data centers, where the Thermal Kit and Thermal Fabric combine thermoelectric cooling chips with embedded control firmware that the company markets as API-accessible and Redfish-compatible, delivering millisecond thermal response plus real-time telemetry and analytics. Phononic publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification; technical access runs through sales and customer support.

providers.name: Praxis AI (Vortexify)
providers.description: Praxis AI is a Y Combinator (Fall 2024) company that now operates as Vortexify (vortexify.ai). Vortexify is an AI-native platform that generates operational software directly from a company's data: teams connect data sources through 20+ prebuilt connectors (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, BigQuery, Redshift, Snowflake, NetSuite, Oracle, S3, Azure Blob, Google Sheets/Drive, SharePoint and more), describe requirements in plain English, and AI agents plan, code, test and deploy backend logic plus custom frontends with no infrastructure to manage. The platform emphasizes building complete apps on operational data rather than just dashboards, with built-in scheduling, serverless compute execution, role-based access control, audit logs, sandboxed environments, token-based authentication, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. Praxis AI was founded by Aditya Tewari (ex-Palantir) and Ransika Liyanage (ex-Tesla, GM, Deloitte), originally focused on manufacturing-specific AI agents for predicting and preventing machine failures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator. Vortexify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Last Energy
providers.description: Last Energy is an American developer and operator of micro-modular nuclear power plants, founded in 2019 in Washington, D.C. by Bret Kugelmass as a commercial spinout of the Energy Impact Center. Its flagship PWR-20 is a 20 MWe pressurized water reactor assembled from a few dozen factory-made, steel-encased modules that ship to site and are installed rather than constructed in place. Last Energy sells power rather than reactors: it designs, finances, owns and operates plants under long-term power purchase agreements for energy-intensive customers including data centers, metals, chemicals, cement, pulp and paper, and food and beverage. The company has announced projects in Texas, South Wales, Poland and Romania, entered nuclear site licensing in the United Kingdom, partnered with Texas A&M and DP World, and raised roughly $164M across a $40M Series B and a $100M Series C. Last Energy publishes a marketing site and a gated customer/whitepaper portal, but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Lightship
providers.description: Lightship is an American manufacturer of all-electric travel trailers, co-founded by former Tesla leaders Toby Kraus and Ben Parker, with design and manufacturing in Colorado and offices in San Francisco. Its flagship product, the AE.1, is marketed as the first mass-produced all-electric travel trailer, offering up to 77 kWh of battery capacity, 1.8 kW of integrated solar, and named technologies including TrekDrive self-propulsion, CampQuiet silent operation, and Aero-Electric Design. Owners control the trailer through an onboard Atlas tablet and companion mobile app. Lightship sells direct to consumer and states that more than 85% of its supply chain is in the United States. Enrichment probes on 2026-07-19 found no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this is a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API listing.

providers.name: OSARO
providers.description: OSARO is a San Francisco-based industrial AI company that builds machine-learning software for warehouse and fulfillment robotics. Its SightWorks perception platform and AutoModel learning system let industrial robot arms perceive, grasp and place highly variable goods without per-SKU pre-training, 3D object models or fixed programming, powering piece picking, robotic bagging, kitting and mixed-case depalletizing in production deployments across five countries. OSARO sells complete robotic work cells and licenses its perception software to robot makers and system integrators, wrapping deployments in its HyperCare support program. The company publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; integration with customer estates (WMS/WCS, conveyors, ASRS, AMRs) is delivered as a professional-services engagement through OSARO and its integrator partners rather than through a self-serve API.

providers.name: Beyond Limits
providers.description: Beyond Limits (trading as BeyondAI) is an enterprise and industrial artificial intelligence company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Glendale, California, built on cognitive and neuro-symbolic AI technology licensed from Caltech and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Its Hybrid AI Platform combines machine learning, generative AI and rule-based symbolic reasoning so that industrial operators get explainable, auditable recommendations instead of black-box predictions. Products include the Hybrid AI Platform (with Data, ML Ops/PRE, KB Ops and a low-code API available under a development license), Operations Advisor, Beyond Search generative AI, AI in a Box on-premises infrastructure, and DocLink document process automation from its Altec subsidiary. The company sells into energy and LNG, oil and gas, refining, petrochemicals, utilities, mining, manufacturing, aerospace and critical infrastructure. Beyond Limits publishes no public developer portal, API reference or self-service sign-up; platform API access is granted to licensed customers, so there is no publicly discoverable machine-readable contract for this provider.

providers.name: Bosch
providers.description: Bosch is a German multinational engineering and technology company producing automotive components, industrial technology, consumer goods, and energy and building technology. Bosch operates the Bosch IoT Suite, an open IoT platform offering device management, software rollouts, edge services, and IoT data analytics, along with open source contributions to Eclipse Foundation IoT projects.

providers.name: Slate Auto
providers.description: Slate Auto is an American electric-vehicle manufacturer building a radically simple, affordable, and customizable electric pickup truck. Designed in California and Michigan, engineered in Michigan, and assembled in the Midwest, the "Blank Slate" starts around $24,950 and offers roughly 205 miles of range, with interchangeable body panels and 200+ accessories that let owners reconfigure the vehicle over its life (including SUV and Fastback body styles). Slate sells direct through a preorder/reservation model, rejects mandatory feature packages and large touchscreens in favor of durability and owner control, and offers fleet solutions. Backed by General Catalyst. As a consumer automaker, Slate Auto publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures company identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sourceday
providers.description: SourceDay is an AI-driven supplier collaboration and purchase order (PO) management platform for manufacturers and distributors. It synchronizes buyers, suppliers, and ERP systems in real time to prevent supply chain disruptions, automating PO change management, shipment visibility, supplier scorecards, and request-for-quote (RFQ) workflows. SourceDay reports managing more than $5B in quarterly direct spend across 100K+ activated suppliers, with 500+ certified ERP integrations spanning Acumatica, Epicor (Kinetic and Prophet 21), Infor, and NetSuite. Integration is delivered through certified ERP connectors rather than a public self-serve developer API; there is no public API documentation, developer portal, or published OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Tenkara
providers.description: Tenkara is an AI-powered operations and supply chain platform for material manufacturers across food, supplements, cosmetics, chemicals, beverages, and OTC products. The platform automates 75+ workflows spanning supplier sourcing and qualification, procurement, freight and logistics booking, order tracking, and compliance documentation (COA, SDS, and audit records), helping manufacturers find better suppliers faster, prevent delays, and run more efficient operations. Tenkara is backed by True Ventures.

providers.name: Advanced Aircraft Company
providers.description: Advanced Aircraft Company (AAC) is a veteran-owned aerospace manufacturer in Hampton, Virginia, founded in 2017 to build long-endurance hybrid fuel-electric VTOL unmanned aircraft systems for commercial, public-safety and defense missions. Its flagship HAMR (Hybrid Advanced Multi-Rotor) UAS flies 3.5+ hours on gas-electric propulsion, and its Greased Lightning tilt-wing is built on technology licensed from NASA Langley Research Center. AAC is a hardware company with no developer program and no product API; its only public machine-readable surface is the WordPress REST API and an OAuth-gated WordPress MCP Adapter server exposed by its own marketing site.

providers.name: Mosaic Manufacturing
providers.description: Mosaic Manufacturing is a Toronto-based additive manufacturing company building automated, high-volume FFF 3D printing systems for factory-floor production of end-use polymer parts. Its flagship Array platform combines integrated robotics, intelligent scheduling software, and high-performance fused-filament-fabrication printers so manufacturers can cut part costs and run true production at scale. Mosaic also makes the Palette line of multi-material hardware and Canvas (canvas3d.io), a cloud/web software platform for file preparation, color/slice, print scheduling, and fleet management. As of this enrichment pass Mosaic publishes no public product API or OpenAPI-described developer surface; its developer-facing presence is the open-source MosaicManufacturing GitHub organization (3MF tooling, slicer post-processing, and firmware) plus a hosted support/knowledge-base portal.

providers.name: Partsimony
providers.description: Partsimony is an intelligent supply chain platform that helps hardware companies turn engineering designs into manufactured products with less time, cost, and friction. Its software analyzes component designs to recommend manufacturing methods, materials, price estimates, and lead times, then matches each part to the optimal manufacturers inside and outside a company's network — batching components for volume leverage across processes like 3D printing, CNC machining, injection molding, castings, electronics, and assemblies. The platform also coordinates RFPs, proposals, orders, messaging, and payment terms between OEMs and their manufacturing partners. Partsimony operates a web application and product documentation but does not currently publish a public developer API. Founded in 2015 and based in Brooklyn, NY; backed by Techstars.

providers.name: EnerSys
providers.description: EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial applications, manufacturing batteries, chargers, accessories, and outdoor equipment enclosures. EnerSys serves motive power, reserve power, aerospace and defense, and specialty markets. While EnerSys offers a number of customer-facing web tools (Battery Sizing Program, Motive Power configurator, CARB Compliance Calculator) and product-level telemetry such as the Wi-iQ battery monitoring system and NexSys iON connected fleet platform, no public developer APIs or open specifications have been published as of this index.

providers.name: Xage
providers.description: Xage Security is a Palo Alto, California zero trust access and protection company whose Xage Fabric Platform enforces identity-based access control across operational technology (OT), IT, cloud and edge environments — covering privileged access management, secure remote access, VPN replacement, zero trust segmentation, critical asset protection and zero trust data exchange for critical infrastructure operators in energy, utilities, manufacturing, oil and gas, transportation, defense, government and space. Xage also markets a control layer that governs how AI agents reach resources over MCP, A2A and REST APIs. The Fabric Manager exposes a REST API that third-party platforms integrate against, but its reference documentation is published only inside the customer-authenticated Xage support portal.

providers.name: Acerta
providers.description: Acerta (Acerta Analytics Solutions Inc.) is a Canadian industrial-AI company whose LinePulse platform delivers AI-driven manufacturing quality analytics for discrete manufacturing. Founded in 2017 in Kitchener-Waterloo, Ontario, Acerta helps Tier-1 automotive and powertrain manufacturers detect defects early, reduce scrap and rework, and root-cause complex production issues in real time. LinePulse replaces statistical process control software, spreadsheets, and custom querying tools with real-time SPC, predictive monitoring, and machine-learning root-cause analysis, and ingests production data through a proprietary secure ingestion API. The platform is built on Microsoft Azure, is SOC 2 Type 1 certified, and is proven across 300+ production lines in 12 countries with customers including BorgWarner, Dana, Linamar, Ford, ZF, Ballard, and BMW. Acerta is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. Acerta exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, self-serve sign-up, or SDKs; integration is delivered through enterprise deployment with the LinePulse ingestion API.

providers.name: Altara
providers.description: Altara is a deep-tech AI company (seed-stage, $7M, backed by Greylock and Jeff Dean) building an agentic scientific intelligence platform for the physical sciences. Its AI agents reason across fragmented technical data — sensor and instrument time series, wafer maps, inspection images, and experimental records — to accelerate R&D-through-manufacturing workflows such as experimental design, yield analysis, anomaly detection, and failure analysis. Altara unifies siloed data in place without migrations, giving agents full operational context across numerical, text, and image sources for semiconductors, advanced materials, batteries, medical devices, specialty chemicals, and industrials. The platform is SOC 2 Type II compliant with encryption, RBAC, SSO, and self-hosted (VPC) or dedicated single-tenant cloud deployment. Altara does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity and security posture as a lead for future enrichment.

providers.name: JSW One
providers.description: JSW One Platforms is the digital B2B arm of India's JSW Group, operating a full-stack e-commerce and services platform for the country's manufacturing and construction MSMEs. It runs four connected businesses on one technology stack: JSW One Commerce (jswonemsme.com), a multi-brand marketplace for TMT bars, mild/hot-rolled/cold-rolled and structural steel, coated steel, wire rods, cement and bitumen sourced from certified mills; JSW One Homes (jswonehomes.com), a turnkey home-construction service with digital project tracking across fifteen Indian cities; JSW One Finance, the NBFC arm providing digital credit lines, channel financing and invoice factoring to MSMEs and retailers; and private brands JSW One TMT and One Helix. The platform reported FY25 gross merchandise value of INR 12,567 crore across more than 84,000 registered MSMEs, and raised INR 575 crore in a 2025 round led by the State Bank of India. JSW One publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; its customer-facing surfaces are the web marketplace and the JSW One MSME mobile apps. It does publish a maintained llms.txt on both of its consumer properties, plus an explicit AI/LLM bot-access policy on JSW One Homes.

providers.name: Orbital Materials
providers.description: Orbital Materials (rebranded Orbital Industries in 2026) is an AI industrial company founded in 2022 by Jonathan Godwin, a former DeepMind researcher, with offices in London and San Francisco. It applies frontier AI to the discovery, testing and deployment of advanced materials and to the hardware and manufacturing built around them, co-designing materials and hardware together rather than sequentially. Its public technical output is a family of open-source machine-learned interatomic potentials — the Orb, Orb-v2/v3 and OrbMol foundation models for atomic simulation — distributed as the Apache-2.0 licensed `orb-models` Python package on PyPI and GitHub and as model weights on Hugging Face. Its internal platform, CurieOS, and its Orbital IT data-center module business are marketed through a contact form rather than a developer program. The company publishes no public HTTP API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Astronergy
providers.description: Astronergy (Chint New Energy Technology Co., Ltd.) is the photovoltaic cell and module manufacturing arm of China's CHINT Group. Founded in 2006, it is one of the earliest private Chinese enterprises in the PV sector and is ranked among the world's largest module suppliers. It designs, manufactures and sells high-efficiency crystalline-silicon PV cells and modules — notably the n-type TOPCon ASTRO N series in bifacial and monofacial form — for utility-scale power stations, commercial and industrial rooftops, and residential systems. Astronergy sells into more than 140 countries and regions and operates manufacturing bases and sales centers in markets including Germany, Spain, the USA, Brazil and Turkey. Its public web surface is a marketing and product-download site: datasheets, installation manuals, warranty and certification PDFs, a module-authenticity checker and a PV Planner yield calculator. It publishes no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Asseta
providers.description: Asseta is a San Francisco-based online marketplace for the secondary market in semiconductor manufacturing equipment and parts. Founded in 2013, the platform lets fabs, refurbishers, and dealers list and discover used, refurbished, and new components, ranging from chamber assemblies and power supplies to smaller parts like o-rings, with more than 450,000 listings from suppliers around the world. Buyers request quotes from global suppliers with a single click and typically save 50-60% versus OEM pricing. Asseta is a portfolio company of a16z and Y Combinator. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company identity and its published web properties.

providers.name: Formic
providers.description: Formic is a Chicago, Illinois-based Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) company founded in 2020 by Saman Farid that delivers full-service industrial automation to American manufacturers on a pay-per-hour, fixed monthly subscription model with no capital expenditure. Formic specializes in end-of-line manufacturing operations — palletizing, case packing, and robotic pallet wrapping — and pairs deployed robots with a 24/7 remote monitoring, support, and field-service operation. The company's software stack includes Formic Core, an embedded operating system that abstracts motion, vision, sensing, and real-time coordination across heterogeneous industrial robot hardware (Fanuc, ABB, Kuka, Doosan) behind unified control interfaces; Formic Cortex; the Colony 2.0 fleet dashboard; FAST configuration tools; and Formic Production Intelligence (FPI), a manufacturer-facing analytics surface. Formic has raised more than $86M across rounds led by Lux Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and other investors, and works through a network of 100+ system-integrator partners with 500+ systems deployed. Formic's revenue model is the RaaS subscription itself; there is no public developer API, no published SDKs, and no public customer-portal API documentation. Formic Core's "unified APIs" are internal abstractions used by Formic engineers and integrator partners to drive robot hardware — they are not exposed to manufacturers or third-party developers.

providers.name: Kyrok
providers.description: Kyrok GmbH is a Berlin-based software company building an AI operating system for mid-sized pharmaceutical and chemical manufacturers in Europe. The platform layers over a company's existing ERP (SAP S/4HANA, SAP R/3, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Infor, Applus) and connects the systems supply chain teams currently hold together by hand into intelligent operations across customer service, production planning, material planning and procurement. Kyrok positions itself on an "AI assists, people decide" model, running on European infrastructure in Frankfurt am Main, GDPR-compliant, with ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certifications in progress. The company announced a EUR 3.1M round in June 2026 and names AnalytiChem and Konapharma as customers. Kyrok connects to ERP systems via API but publishes no public developer API, API reference, or SDKs as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: AI Build
providers.description: AI Build (Aibuild) is a London and Silicon Valley based software company, founded in 2015, that is transforming additive manufacturing with agentic AI. Its flagship Aibuild OS is an autonomous engineering platform whose computer-use AI operates CAD, CAE, and CAM software the way a human engineer would, carrying work from design intent through to manufacturing-ready output. Aibuild CAM provides toolpathing for large-format and robotic 3D printing, CNC machining, mould design, and analysis, while Aibuild FETS delivers finite element thermomechanical simulation. The company is a portfolio company of Seedcamp and SuperSeed and appears in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Goodfellow
providers.description: Goodfellow (Goodfellow Advanced Materials) is a global specialty-materials supplier founded in 1946 and headquartered in Cambridgeshire, United Kingdom, serving research, prototyping and specialized manufacturing markets in more than 111 countries. Its catalog spans over 70,000 stocked products drawn from 700+ different materials in many forms, including metals, alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites, compounds and glass, alongside custom fabrication and laboratory testing services. Customers include universities, government research facilities, laboratories and advanced manufacturers, served through subsidiaries in the United States, China, France and Germany. Goodfellow was acquired by Battery Ventures in 2021 to help digitize its operations and fund materials acquisitions. Goodfellow is a business-to-business e-commerce and catalog operation; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs or webhooks.

providers.name: CERPRO
providers.description: CERPRO is a Berlin-based industrial software company building AI-powered quality-assurance and process automation for small and medium-sized manufacturers. Its flagship product, QualiSpec, uses computer-vision and large-model AI to automatically extract features, dimensions, tolerances and drill-hole specifications from technical drawings (PDF, JPG, DXF) and generate inspection reports and quality documents in customized templates such as VDA, EMPB and inspection plans. This removes manual copy-paste and data-entry work from quality control, cutting documentation time by up to 70-90% and reducing errors while creating a unified data foundation that connects OEMs and suppliers. Since launching in December 2024 the software has been adopted by more than 100 SMEs across aerospace, medical devices and mechanical engineering. CERPRO is a Techstars portfolio company and raised a ~EUR 2M pre-seed round in 2025. The product is delivered as a cloud SaaS platform (platform.cerpro.io) hosted on AWS in Germany, with an ISO 27001 certified, GDPR/BDSG-compliant data-security posture.

providers.name: Overview
providers.description: Overview (overview.ai) builds AI-powered machine vision systems for manufacturing quality control. Its edge-computing platform runs vision transformer models directly on smart cameras with on-device NVIDIA GPUs to perform automated defect detection, assembly verification, and real-time inspection without cloud dependency. Overview serves connector, semiconductor, packaging, automotive, pharmaceutical, aerospace, renewable energy, food, and textile manufacturers, and integrates with factory-floor systems (PLCs, ERPs, SCADA) over MQTT and digital I/O rather than a public REST API. Backed by GV and Homebrew. Profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Robco
providers.description: RobCo is a Munich- and Austin-based industrial robotics company building software-defined, modular robotic automation delivered as Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) with zero upfront capital expenditure. Its modular robot arms (up to 8 axes, 40 kg payload, 2.5 m reach, 0.1 mm repeatability), the Alfie autonomous robot, the RobFlow no-code programming platform, RobCo Studio configuration and simulation tooling, and the RobVision AI vision system let manufacturers automate machine tending, palletizing, materials handling, and finishing tasks. RobCo serves manufacturing, food and beverage, logistics, automotive, wood, and defense customers, and is backed by Lightspeed, Sequoia Capital, Lingotto, Kindred Capital, and Promus Ventures.

providers.name: TransDigm Group
providers.description: TransDigm Group is a leading global designer, producer, and supplier of highly engineered aerospace components, systems, and subsystems for use on nearly all commercial and military aircraft. The company operates 49 independent operating units producing proprietary, sole-source components including actuation systems, ignition systems, fuel systems, airframe and flight control components, cockpit security systems, seatbelts, airbags, pumps, valves, switches, and cockpit displays. TransDigm serves commercial airlines, defense OEMs, aerospace distributors, and the US Department of Defense.

providers.name: Invisible AI
providers.description: Invisible AI is a next-generation computer vision company delivering a Vision Execution System (VES) for manufacturing. NVIDIA Jetson-powered edge devices with Intel RealSense 3D depth cameras and on-device SSD storage mount to existing factory infrastructure and, within hours, encode and segment the production floor in real time. The no-code, edge-based platform captures 100% of production cycles across every station without wearables, operator disruption, or cloud integration, then analyzes human motion and objects to surface cycle-time variability, process drift, quality escapes, and safety/ergonomics risk. Founded in 2018 by autonomous-vehicle veterans and backed by Sierra Ventures, it serves automotive and aerospace OEMs including Toyota, Ford, General Motors, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and Nissan. Invisible AI publishes no public API or developer platform today; this profile captures its company identity, security posture, and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Northrop Grumman
providers.description: Northrop Grumman Corporation is a US global aerospace, defense and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, organized into four segments: Aeronautics Systems, Defense Systems, Mission Systems and Space Systems. It builds autonomous aircraft, strategic bombers and long-range strike weapons, missile defense and integrated battle command systems, radar and electronic warfare sensors, cyber and command-and-control mission software, solid rocket motors, and space vehicles and launch systems for US Department of Defense, intelligence-community, NASA and allied customers. It publishes no public developer program, API portal or machine-readable API contract; its external integration surfaces are the ADFS-authenticated OASIS supplier tools on myngc.com, available only to registered suppliers under contract.

providers.name: Tutor Intelligence
providers.description: Tutor Intelligence builds AI-powered robotic workers for industrial and logistics operations, delivered as robots-as-a-service. Its flagship Cassie palletizing robot handles material-handling tasks — palletizing, depalletizing, and case picking — in warehouses and factories without facility retrofits, and a humanoid robot, Sonny, is slated for late 2026. The company pairs on-robot autonomy with a human-in-the-loop teleoperation and data model, priced per robot-hour with no long-term contracts, and is backed by Union Square Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface is published as of this profiling; the company's public GitHub organization hosts internal tooling and open-source forks rather than a first-party product API.

providers.name: Epicor
providers.description: Epicor Software Corporation provides industry-specific enterprise resource planning software for manufacturing, distribution, retail, and service industries. Epicor Kinetic, the flagship ERP platform, exposes an Open REST API built on OData v4 that gives developers service-based access to all business objects, processes, reports, BAQs, and Epicor Functions using standard HTTP methods and API key authentication.

providers.name: Rimac Automobili
providers.description: Rimac Automobili d.o.o. is a Croatian electric hypercar manufacturer and automotive technology company founded by Mate Rimac in 2009 and headquartered at the Rimac Campus in Kerestinec, near Zagreb. It designs and builds the Nevera and Nevera R all-electric hypercars, and develops the vehicle software, infotainment, connectivity and telemetry stack that runs them in-house. Since the 2021 formation of the Bugatti Rimac joint venture with Porsche, the group's component and OEM-supply business was carved out into the sister company Rimac Technology, while Rimac Automobili remains the vehicle brand. Rimac operates a private, customer-only connected-vehicle backend — an MQTT-based telemetry platform feeding first-party iOS and Android owner apps with location, charging, battery and driving-performance data, plus over-the-air update and remote command channels — but it publishes no public developer program, developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract of any kind. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and portfolio tracking.

providers.name: Robotiq
providers.description: Robotiq designs and manufactures collaborative robotics hardware and software — adaptive grippers, vacuum grippers, force-torque sensors, wrist cameras, and pre-engineered workcells for palletizing, machine tending, screwdriving, and assembly. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lévis, Quebec, Canada, the company helps manufacturers automate repetitive tasks by embedding task intelligence ("Intelligence Made Physical") directly into end-of-arm tooling for platforms such as Universal Robots, FANUC CRX, and Omron/Techman. Robotiq publishes open-source ROS drivers and a C++ gripper SDK through its GitHub organization, but it does not operate a public web/REST API — this profile captures its developer-facing identity, open-source SDKs, and domain security posture rather than a hosted API surface.

providers.name: Valmont Industries
providers.description: Valmont Industries is a global leader in producing fabricated metal products, designing and manufacturing engineered support structures for infrastructure (utility poles, lighting, traffic), mechanized irrigation equipment (Valley center pivot systems), and industrial coatings services. Valmont's Valley brand is the world's leading manufacturer of center pivot and linear irrigation systems, with digital platforms including AgSense 365 and BaseStation3 providing remote monitoring and control of irrigation pivots.

providers.name: Valspar
providers.description: The Valspar Corporation was a global manufacturer of paints and coatings founded in 1806 before being acquired by Sherwin-Williams in 2017 for approximately $11.3 billion. Valspar continues to operate as a brand within Sherwin-Williams, offering consumer paints, industrial coatings, and protective coatings. Digital tools include color visualizers, virtual painters, and color consultation services. No public developer API is available; color and product integrations are available through Sherwin-Williams' partner programs including BIMsmith and Autodesk Revit.

providers.name: American Axle and Manufacturing
providers.description: American Axle & Manufacturing (AAM), now operating as Dauch Corporation following the February 2026 acquisition of Dowlais Group (GKN Automotive and GKN Powder Metallurgy), is a global Tier 1 automotive supplier designing, engineering, and manufacturing driveline and metal forming technologies for electric, hybrid, and internal combustion vehicles. AAM operates an iSupplier Portal for supplier communication, EDI integration for forecasts and releases, and the Demand AAM aftermarket parts portal.

providers.name: Forterro
providers.description: Forterro is a pan-European industrial software company, founded in 2012 and headquartered in London, that provides enterprise resource planning (ERP) and specialised business software to the industrial mid-market. Built through a series of acquisitions, Forterro operates a portfolio of regional and vertical ERP brands - including Abas, Jeeves, Garp, Proconcept, Sylob, Silog, Myfactory, Orderwise, Clipper, 123Insight, BPSC, Helios, Proffix, Prodaso and its cloud-native Fortee product - alongside best-in-class point solutions such as warehouse management (WMS), point of sale (POS), material requirements planning (MRP) and business intelligence. The company serves more than 13,000 industrial businesses across manufacturing, warehousing, wholesale and retail from 40+ offices worldwide.

providers.name: HZO
providers.description: HZO is a protective coating company specializing in Parylene and thin-film conformal coatings that safeguard electronics from moisture, humidity, salt fog, corrosion, and harsh chemicals. Founded in Salt Lake City and now headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, HZO delivers turnkey coating services and manufacturing solutions across consumer electronics, automotive and mobility, industrial, medical device, IoT, and battery markets, with coating facilities and centers of excellence in the United States, Hungary, China, and Vietnam. HZO is a physical-materials and contract-manufacturing business ("Protection from the Inside Out") rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract. This profile records the public web hygiene surface it does serve — an llms.txt discovery file, an RFC 9116 security.txt, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Alcoa
providers.description: Alcoa Corporation is a global industry leader in bauxite, alumina, and aluminum production. Founded in 1888, Alcoa operates mines, refineries, and smelters across Australia, Brazil, Canada, Iceland, Norway, Saudi Arabia, and the United States. The company is a Fortune 500 member and one of the world's largest aluminum producers, supplying lightweight, high-strength materials to automotive, aerospace, packaging, construction, and industrial markets. Alcoa is committed to sustainability through low-carbon aluminum production, responsible bauxite mining, and advancing aluminum recycling.

providers.name: Drag Bot
providers.description: drag&bot is a web-based industrial robotics software platform for the intuitive setup, programming, and operation of industrial robots without prior robotics or coding skills. Founded in Stuttgart in 2016 and acquired by KEBA in 2021, it lets production workers assemble robot programs by dragging and dropping reusable Function Blocks. The platform is built on ROS (Robot Operating System), making it vendor-neutral across robot brands such as KUKA, ABB, Universal Robots, FANUC, Denso, Kinova, and Aubo, as well as a wide range of grippers and peripheral tools. Developers extend the platform with Python/JSON Function Blocks and ROS-based Components (hardware drivers), and integrate with factory equipment over Modbus TCP/IP and MQTT. drag&bot has been integrated into KEBA's Kemro X automation platform. Its programmatic surface is exposed as ROS services, topics, and messages rather than a public REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Heven AeroTech
providers.description: Heven AeroTech (formerly Heven Drones) is a Dulles, Virginia headquartered manufacturer of hydrogen fuel-cell powered, runway-independent unmanned aircraft systems built for defense, national security and public safety missions. Founded in 2019, the company designs its own hydrogen propulsion stack and ships six named airframes — Raider, Z1, H2D55, Refueler, Atlas and Urban X — marketed on multi-hour endurance, low thermal and acoustic signature, and rapid payload and hydrogen-tank swaps. The Z1 is listed as a Blue UAS Select platform and the H2D55, Raider and Z1 are advertised as NDAA compliant. Heven operates sites in Dulles VA, Bingen WA, Mevo Carmel Israel and Mumbai India, and raised a $100M Series B led by IonQ. Heven AeroTech is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Markt Pilot (aka MP)
providers.description: MARKT-PILOT GmbH is a German software company (registered in Beilstein, business address Stuttgart, with a US office in Chicago) that provides a unified pricing performance platform for industrial manufacturers. Its flagship product, MP ONE, combines an Intelligence Engine (real-time competitor and market data with AI-powered cross-reference part matching), a Decision Engine (cost-plus, market-based, and attribute-based pricing workflows), and a Performance Engine (portfolio, revenue, and margin analysis with executive dashboards). MARKT-PILOT serves 200+ manufacturers across agriculture, construction and mining, machine tooling, packaging, and industrial equipment, helping them move from static annual spare-parts pricing to dynamic, data-driven pricing. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. The company operates a marketing site, blog, and a hosted (Better Stack) status page, but publishes no public developer/API surface: no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, well-known discovery endpoints, or client SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: CNC24
providers.description: CNC24 is a German online manufacturing platform for ordering custom CNC parts and precision components. Customers upload CAD files (STEP, STP, DWG, DXF, PDF and 3D data) and receive a binding quote within 48 hours, with production routed through a vetted network of 500+ manufacturers across 21 countries and roughly 5,500 machines. An AI-powered matching algorithm assigns each request to partners with the right expertise and production environment. Supported processes include CNC milling, turning, laser and waterjet cutting, sheet metal bending, punching, EDM, 3D printing, injection molding and die casting, serving aerospace, automotive, medical, robotics, construction and energy customers. The platform runs a fully digital workflow from quoting to delivery with order tracking, ISO 9001:2015 quality assurance, AES-256 encryption and anonymized drawings shared with partners. CNC24 is a Seedcamp portfolio company. No public developer API, SDKs or API documentation are published.

providers.name: Instrumental
providers.description: Instrumental is a platform for manufacturing intelligence that helps companies detect and prevent product failures during the manufacturing process. The Instrumental API enables programmatic access to retrieve unit and inspection test data and metadata from Instrumental projects.

providers.name: NACCO Industries
providers.description: NACCO Industries is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The NACCO Industries API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Operon
providers.description: Operon is an AI-powered manufacturing intelligence platform (Y Combinator S2026) that turns P&IDs (Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams), schematics, datasheets, and scanned engineering documents into one structured, queryable model of a plant. Its P&ID Recognition detects equipment, instruments, valves, and piping symbols across ISA, ISO, and proprietary symbology; its P&ID Agent generates standards-compliant diagrams from text, simulation data, or sketches; and Knowledge Chat lets engineers query plant documentation in natural language and build agentic workflows for safety, compliance, HAZOP/PHA, EHS, material take-offs, brownfield digitization, and management-of-change. Operon exports structured DEXPI data and offers cloud and on-premise deployment with encryption, role-based access control, and audit trails. As of July 2026 the product is in private beta (pid.operonsolutions.com) and publishes no public API.

providers.name: Smartex
providers.description: Smartex is an AI and computer-vision company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Porto, Portugal that builds hardware-enabled software for the textile manufacturing industry. Its systems inspect fabric in real time on the knitting machine to detect defects at the source, cutting textile waste, CO2 emissions, water, energy and rework. The product suite spans CORE (a machine-vision inspection add-on for circular knitting machines), FACT (an all-in-one digital factory-management platform for production visibility and quality control) and LOOP (supply-chain communication and traceability). Smartex is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, DCVC, Tony Fadell's Build Collective, H&M Group, SOSV/HAX, Spider Capital, Momenta Ventures and Fashion for Good. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; customer access is through the FACT platform login. This profile was surfaced from the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from Smartex's public web surface.

providers.name: xTool
providers.description: xTool is a Shenzhen-based digital-fabrication brand, spun out of Makeblock and backed by HongShan, making CO2, fiber, and diode laser cutters and engravers, laser welders, and DTF printers for makers and small businesses, driven by its xTool Creative Space (XCS) desktop software. xTool sells through a Shopify storefront and runs a support and academy portal, a user community, and the Atomm maker-project platform, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Aletiq
providers.description: Aletiq is a French software company building a next-generation, AI-powered Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Product Data Management (PDM) platform for regulated manufacturers. The platform centralizes technical data (CAD files, drawings, bills of materials, configurations, and work instructions), enforces traceability and regulatory compliance, and automates business processes such as approvals, engineering change management, and project milestones. Aletiq emphasizes rapid deployment and high adoption across operational teams, and integrates with major CAD tools (SolidWorks, CATIA, Autodesk Inventor, Siemens NX, Creo) and ERP systems (SAP, Sage, Cegid, Infor, Odoo) via connectors and a custom-integration API. It serves aerospace and defense, medical devices, energy, electronics, automotive, and luxury-goods industries. Aletiq is backed by Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead profile.

providers.name: Bright Machines
providers.description: Bright Machines is a San Francisco-based software-defined manufacturing company founded in 2018 by Amar Hanspal and Lior Susan that builds a full-stack intelligent automation platform for electronics and AI-infrastructure assembly. Its Microfactory pairs modular Bright Robotic Cells with Brightware, a platform operating system that orchestrates hardware, runs a machine-vision "Smart Skills" perception stack, and provides manufacturing-execution services for work orders, material management and real-time production KPIs. Bright Data, the company's data layer, unifies component, process and enterprise-system data through secure APIs and auditable data flows, and Bright Designer turns product CAD into assembly-ready digital twins using NVIDIA Omniverse on Microsoft Azure. The company has raised roughly $279M from Eclipse, BlackRock, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Jabil and others. All platform and data interfaces are delivered to customers under commercial engagement; Bright Machines publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: Kraka
providers.description: Kraka Technologies GmbH is a Berlin-based industrial AI company whose platform turns plain video recordings of shop-floor tasks into standardized, multilingual, step-by-step work instructions. Kraka Studio is the core product, extended by Training, Maintenance and Quality modules covering workforce qualification, AI-assisted fault diagnosis and checklist-driven quality control. Kraka positions itself as closing the execution gap between ERP systems that manage data and the work actually performed on the factory floor. Backed by Seedcamp. No public API, developer portal or SDK is published as of July 2026.

providers.name: LaborUp
providers.description: LaborUp is an AI-powered recruiting platform for American manufacturing, connecting skilled industrial workers — machinists, CNC programmers, welders, and maintenance technicians — with manufacturing employers. The platform combines voice-first AI screening, skills verification, and constraint-aware matching with dedicated recruiter support, and claims 5-10x faster hiring, more than 50% lower cost than traditional staffing agencies, 3x better post-hire retention, and a proprietary network of 25,000+ vetted workers. Founded by Simba Jonga, LaborUp raised $7.74M ($1.935M pre-seed plus a $5.8M seed announced in August 2025) led by NVP with Torch Capital, Threshold, Heartland VC, Daybreak, Westbound, Marketplace Capital, and Market Square Ventures. Early traction is concentrated in the Knoxville, Tennessee manufacturing corridor and in aerospace, shipbuilding, and critical infrastructure. As of July 2026 LaborUp publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification; the product is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application.

providers.name: Verve Motion
providers.description: Verve Motion is a wearable robotics company spun out of the Harvard Biodesign Lab that builds SafeLift, a soft powered exosuit for industrial workers who lift repetitively. Inertial sensors woven into the suit detect lifting motion and trigger assistive force that the company says takes up to 40% of the strain off a worker's back, while Verve Logic — its cloud platform — collects the resulting movement data and reports ergonomic risk, unsafe-posture trends and exosuit utilization to safety managers. SafeLift is sold as a subscription bundling the exosuit, the Verve Logic data portal and Verve Care support, and is distributed in part through partners such as HexArmor. Verve Motion publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the Verve Logic portal at logic.vervemotion.com is a customer-only single-page application that disallows crawling in robots.txt.

providers.name: Fetch Robotics
providers.description: Fetch Robotics is a provider of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for the manufacturing, distribution, and fulfillment industries, enabling customers to optimize warehouse and material-handling workflows through robotic automation. Its Fetch and Freight robots are programmed through a ROS (Robot Operating System) interface — standard ROS topics, services, and actions conforming to ROS Enhancement Proposals (REPs) — rather than an HTTP/REST API, and the first-party client, driver, and simulation libraries are published as open source in the fetchrobotics GitHub organization. Fetch Robotics was acquired by Zebra Technologies in August 2021 for approximately $290M; fetchrobotics.com now redirects to Zebra and the autonomous-mobile-robot product line is being wound down (2025-2026), though the open-source ROS packages remain available.

providers.name: Kaavio
providers.description: Kaavio is an AI-powered product content platform for B2B distributors and manufacturers. It sources product data from supplier submissions, PDFs, spec sheets, internal systems (PIM, DAM, ERP) and the web, validates it with conflict detection and confidence scoring, generates market-ready content (structured attributes, SEO descriptions, FAQs, comparisons, substitutes), and deploys it to destination systems such as PIMs, e-commerce platforms, and channels. The platform handles catalogs ranging from 20,000 to more than a million SKUs and claims a 90% reduction in the time and effort to get market-ready SKU content online. Founded by Derek Gregg and Sam Bobb, based in San Francisco, and backed by Baukunst, Techstars, and Looking Glass Capital ($2.9M pre-seed).

providers.name: Kaman Corporation
providers.description: Kaman Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Kaman Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Nth Cycle
providers.description: Nth Cycle is a critical mineral refining company headquartered in Beverly, Massachusetts, that recovers production-grade nickel, cobalt, copper and rare earth elements from mined ore, low-grade tailings and recycled industrial scrap. Its patented OYSTER platform uses electro-extraction — an alternative to conventional hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy that combines electrochemistry, filtration and chemical precipitation into a single continuous, closed-loop architecture — to deliver modular refining at roughly 70% lower capital intensity, 75% less waste, and economic viability at 5-10x smaller scale than a centralized refinery. Systems install inside existing buildings and can be deployed in as little as two years including permitting, under licensing, build-own-operate tolling, or multi-feedstock off-take models. The company operates the first domestic commercial-scale nickel and cobalt scrap refining system in Fairfield, Ohio, holds a $1.1 billion offtake agreement with Trafigura, was selected by the U.S. Department of Energy for award negotiations of up to $100 million toward a new critical mineral refining facility, and has announced a NYSE listing via business combination with Kensington Capital Acquisition Corp. VI. Enrichment probing on 2026-08-26 found no public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger/GraphQL/AsyncAPI contract, developer portal, SDK or package-registry entry, CLI, MCP server, A2A agent card, gRPC/Protobuf or WSDL contract, webhook surface, or served /.well-known document — Nth Cycle is a materials refining company, not an API provider.

providers.name: Sanctuary AI
providers.description: Sanctuary AI is a Vancouver, British Columbia humanoid robotics company on a mission to create and deploy industrial-grade general-purpose humanoid robots to help address growing labor challenges. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for dull, dirty, and dangerous work in automotive, manufacturing, and logistics environments. Phoenix is driven by Carbon, Sanctuary AI's proprietary AI control system that mimics human cognitive subsystems — memory, sight, sound, and touch — to translate natural-language tasks into dexterous physical actions. The company is vertically integrated, designing everything from motors and actuators through to generative AI algorithms in-house. Co-founded by James Wells (CEO) and Olivia Norton (CTO/CPO), Sanctuary AI has a private GitHub organization with no public repositories, no developer portal, no public API, no SDK, and no published OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications. The commercial model is hardware sales and enterprise deployments; Carbon is a proprietary on-board system and there is no public developer surface.

providers.name: Westlake Chemical
providers.description: Westlake Chemical (now Westlake Corporation) is a global manufacturer and supplier of petrochemicals, polymers, building products, and specialty chemicals. The company produces ethylene, polyethylene, PVC, chlor-alkali, epoxy resins, and fabricated building products serving packaging, healthcare, automotive, consumer goods, and construction markets worldwide.

providers.name: Fashinza
providers.description: Fashinza is a tech-enabled apparel manufacturing and supply-chain platform that connects fashion brands and retailers with a vetted global network of garment manufacturers. It streamlines end-to-end production: sourcing designs and fabrics, AI-powered supplier matching, tech-pack and sample creation, real-time production tracking, quality control, and merchandising and forecasting support so brands can move from design to delivery in shortened 30-45 day cycles. Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures, the company operates a buyer login and a supplier onboarding surface but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: KLA
providers.description: KLA Corporation (formerly KLA-Tencor) is a leader in process control and process-enabling solutions for manufacturing wafers and reticles, integrated circuits, packaging, printed circuit boards and flat panel displays. KLA delivers advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, and computational analytics for the semiconductor industry. KLA does not publish a public developer portal or open API program; customer-facing software and tool APIs are provided to KLA customers under contract and are not publicly available.

providers.name: Turing Labs
providers.description: Turing Labs (turingsaas.com) is a product-led growth platform for consumer packaged goods companies. Its "Growth OS" helps CPG and consumer-product teams pressure-test which product bets will win before spending, perfect formulations, and fund launches from recovered margin, consolidating product development, formulation R&D, and go-to-market decisioning into a single engine rather than a stack of disconnected tools. The company is backed by Insight Partners and Menlo Ventures. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface was found during enrichment; the product is delivered through a login-gated web application at app.turingsaas.com.

providers.name: CelLink
providers.description: CelLink (CelLink Technologies / CelLink Corporation) manufactures large-format, high-conductance flexible circuits that consolidate power, data, and sensing into thin, lightweight layers, replacing traditional wire harnesses and busbars. Its product lines are Battery Pack Interconnect, Flex Harness, and Data Center power delivery, serving automotive, aerospace, industrial, data center, and grid-storage electrification markets. Founded by CEO Kevin Coakley and VP Engineering Malcolm Brown, the company is headquartered in San Carlos, California, with sites in Georgetown, Texas; Wixom, Michigan; Hamburg, Germany; and Shanghai, China. CelLink circuits have been in electric-vehicle production since 2020. CelLink is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Euler Motors
providers.description: Euler Motors is an Indian electric commercial vehicle manufacturer headquartered in New Delhi, building battery-electric cargo and light commercial vehicles for last-mile logistics — the HiLoad and Turbo electric three-wheelers and the Storm EV four-wheeler light commercial vehicle range. Alongside the vehicles the company operates Euler Shepherd, a connected-vehicle telematics platform delivered as two end-user products: Shepherd Lite (a mobile app for real-time vehicle location, battery state of charge, range, charging status and alerts) and Shepherd Enterprise (a browser-based fleet console with trip, utilization and operations reporting). Euler Motors publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog or partner integration documentation on any host it controls. The Shepherd web console is a single-page application whose backend answers anonymous requests with 403, so the telematics data surface is reachable only to vehicle owners inside the product. The company does publish an llms.txt at its web root, directing AI crawlers to its product, service-network and blog pages.

providers.name: Modern Meadow
providers.description: Modern Meadow is a bio-design and materials-science company founded in 2011 in Brooklyn by Andras Forgacs, Francoise Marga, Gabor Forgacs and Karoly Jakab, now headquartered in Nutley / Pine Brook, New Jersey, where it operates an innovation lab opened in 2017. The company applies synthetic biology and protein engineering to build animal-free, bio-fabricated alternatives to leather and other petrochemical-derived materials, through the Bio-Alloy technology platform (an alloy of engineered proteins and bio-based polymers), the BIO-VERA material launched in 2023, and its current flagship INNOVERA, a next-generation leather alternative made from plant proteins, biopolymers and recycled rubber with more than 80% renewable carbon content. It sells into interiors, fashion and accessories, footwear, and automotive, and has partnered with BASF, tannery HELLER-LEDER (a 2026 European joint venture) and Allbirds (the Terralux footwear line). Modern Meadow has raised roughly $236M. It is a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: profiling on 2026-08-01 found no public API, no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI/GraphQL/MCP surface, no /.well-known/ documents, and no GitHub organization. Its corporate site (modernmeadow.com, Craft CMS) largely redirects to the product site innovera-world.com.

providers.name: MyWear
providers.description: MyWear (operating as vPersonalize Inc.) is a Houston, Texas based, Accel-backed software company founded in 2014 that provides a cloud platform for on-demand apparel manufacturing and mass customization. Its integrated toolset spans the full production lifecycle: a 3D product customizer and 3D uniform builder for real-time design, an online pattern-making CAD with automated size grading, web-to-print and print-layout automation with color management (PANTONE, CMYK, custom SPOT), an automated catalog builder, e-commerce storefront integration, and order and factory management across multiple suppliers. The company holds six US patents covering its automation and pattern-generation technology and targets apparel brands, sportswear makers, and print-on-demand operators. The public surface is a marketing and product site (vpersonalize.com); no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Polymateria
providers.description: Polymateria Ltd is a British materials-science company, based at the Imperial College I-HUB on the White City Campus in London, that develops Biotransformation — a masterbatch additive blended into polyethylene and polypropylene at roughly 2% by weight so that plastic which escapes a waste stream weathers into a bioavailable wax and fully biodegrades in the open environment without leaving microplastics behind. The company co-authored BSI PAS 9017, the first standard for measuring the biodegradability of polyolefins, is a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer and a Terra Carta signatory, and sells to converters, brand owners and packaging manufacturers rather than to developers. Its product is a chemical additive, not software: the public website is a WordPress marketing and media site, and the only credentialed surface it operates is a customer portal that serves third-party test datasets as documents. No developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind was found in this pass.

providers.name: Saphlux
providers.description: Saphlux is a quantum dot Micro-LED (QD-MLED) display technology company founded in 2014 out of Yale University and headquartered in San Diego, California, with additional operations in China and Japan. It commercialized semi-polar (20-21) GaN-on-sapphire epitaxial wafers to address efficiency droop and the green gap in nitride emitters, and now mass-produces NPQD quantum-dot Micro-LED devices.
