providers.description: Electra (legal name Electrasteel, Inc.) is a Boulder, Colorado clean-industrial company founded in 2020 that is reinventing ironmaking. Instead of smelting iron ore with fossil fuels in a blast furnace, Electra uses an electrochemical process — an acidic leach plus electrowinning driven by renewable electricity — to dissolve a broad range of iron ores, including low-grade and previously uncommercialized ores, and plate out 99% pure iron at roughly 60°C while recovering high-value co-minerals and emitting oxygen. The modular design lets units be added as building blocks for rapid scaling and lets the process follow intermittent renewable power. Electra has raised over $200M from Rio Tinto, BHP Ventures, POSCO, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, Capricorn and Lowercarbon Capital, runs a pilot plant in Boulder, and is building a demonstration plant in Colorado. It is an industrial manufacturer with no public developer program: as of this profile it publishes no API, developer portal, documentation, machine-readable specification, or /.well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Newlight Technologies
providers.description: Newlight Technologies, Inc. is a Huntington Beach, California biotechnology company founded in 2003 and incorporated in Delaware that produces AirCarbon, a PHB biomaterial made by naturally-occurring ocean microorganisms that consume air and greenhouse gas. The company operates a commercial-scale biomanufacturing plant and sells AirCarbon as resin to industrial partners and as finished goods under the Restore foodware and Covalent fashion-accessory brands, positioning the material as a carbon-negative, home-compostable, ocean-degradable replacement for petroleum plastic. Newlight is a materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no API reference and no machine-readable contract. Its only agent-reachable surface is the Wix platform Site MCP endpoint that its marketing site advertises in its own llms.txt.

providers.name: USA Rare Earth
providers.description: USA Rare Earth, Inc. (Nasdaq: USAR) is an American critical-minerals and advanced-materials company building a domestic mine-to-magnet rare earth supply chain. It operates a 310,000 sq. ft. sintered neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) permanent magnet manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma, and holds the Round Top heavy rare earth and critical minerals deposit in Hudspeth County, West Texas. The company produces rare earth elements, oxides, metals and sintered permanent magnets for defense, automotive, robotics, industrial and clean-energy customers, with the stated aim of reducing U.S. dependence on offshore rare earth processing and magnet production. It is a materials producer and manufacturer, not a software or data company, and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Emerson Electric
providers.description: Emerson Electric is a Fortune 500 global automation leader with more than 135 years of innovation history. Its portfolio spans automation systems, discrete automation, final control, measurement instrumentation, and test and measurement, marketed through brands such as Fisher, Rosemount, DeltaV, Micro Motion, ASCO, Bettis, PACSystems, Flexim, and NI. Emerson serves industries including power, oil and gas, chemical, life sciences, food and beverage, automotive, data centers, mining, and marine. This repository captures the public APIs, developer resources, and machine-readable artifacts associated with Emerson Electric.

providers.name: Reliance Steel & Aluminum
providers.description: Reliance Steel & Aluminum Co. is the largest metals service center in North America, providing value-added metals processing services and distributing a full line of metal products including aluminum, brass, bronze, carbon and alloy steel, copper, titanium, and stainless steel. Operating over 300 service center locations across 40 US states and 13 countries, Reliance serves more than 130,000 customers across aerospace, automotive, defense, energy, electronics, construction, and semiconductor end markets.

providers.name: Cyngn
providers.description: Cyngn (NASDAQ: CYN) is a Mountain View, California autonomous vehicle technology company that develops and deploys industrial autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for material handling. Its flagship DriveMod stack is a vehicle-agnostic, AI-powered autonomy system that retrofits onto standard industrial vehicles such as tuggers and forklifts, paired with the Cyngn Insight fleet-management, teleoperation, and analytics platform and the Cyngn Evolve data toolkit — together marketed as the Enterprise Autonomy Suite. Cyngn targets warehousing, manufacturing, and logistics operators facing labor shortages and safety challenges, and integrates with major warehouse management systems (Manhattan, Blue Yonder, SAP EWM). The company traces its corporate lineage to Cyanogen Inc. (the CyanogenMod company), whose dormant GitHub organization still links to cyngn.com.

providers.name: Koska
providers.description: KOSKA Corporation (株式会社KOSKA) is a Tokyo-based manufacturing technology company, founded in October 2018, that applies cost accounting and IoT to the Japanese factory floor. Its flagship product GenKan (原価管理自動化サービス) automates cost management for high-mix low-volume manufacturers: RFID and power sensors installed on existing equipment capture work progress and consumption without changing operator behavior, then make processing cost, material cost, and electricity cost visible line by line, feeding real actual-cost figures and KPI setting back to the shop floor and management. A second product, ながら記録 (Nagara Kiroku / "vScribe"), is an AI record-keeping app for manufacturing, construction, and logistics sites — photograph a paper form and AI generates the input form, then operators record hands-free by speaking, with the AI parsing natural speech into structured records, inspections, and reports. KOSKA is led by CEO Kenichiro Sone (Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2021) and advised by Hiroshi Obata, former chair of the Japan Cost Accounting Association. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — it is a sensor-and-SaaS product company, not an API provider.

providers.name: morewis
providers.description: Morewis (摩尔元数) is a Chinese industrial software company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Xiamen, Fujian, that develops cloud-based Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for the manufacturing sector. Its Morewis Cloud industrial internet platform, MoreDEV low-code development platform (including the WisIDE cloud IDE), and MoreAgent / N³ industrial AI large model let manufacturers build and run smart-factory applications with reduced hand coding. Reference clients include Haier, Hisense, Aisino, Inspur, and 3Trees Group. The company raised a ~100M yuan Series B led by Qiming Venture Partners. No public English-language REST API, OpenAPI, SDK, or GitHub organization was found; the developer surface is a China-hosted low-code industrial application platform.

providers.name: Autoliv
providers.description: Autoliv is the world's largest automotive safety supplier, designing, manufacturing, and selling airbags, seatbelts, steering wheels, inflators, pyrotechnic actuators, and related safety electronics for vehicle manufacturers worldwide. The company operates in 25 countries with 13 technology centers and serves all major OEMs.

providers.name: Covariant
providers.description: Covariant is an Emeryville, California warehouse-robotics AI company founded in 2017 (originally as Embodied Intelligence) by UC Berkeley professor Pieter Abbeel and his former students Peter Chen, Rocky Duan, and Tianhao Zhang. The company builds the Covariant Brain, a universal AI platform that enables industrial picking robots to handle virtually any SKU regardless of shape, size, or packaging, and in March 2024 it introduced RFM-1 (Robotics Foundation Model 1), an 8-billion-parameter multimodal transformer trained on text, images, video, robot actions, and numerical sensor readings to give robots human-like reasoning over the physical world. Covariant ships AI-powered solutions for order picking, sortation, item induction, kitting, depalletization, and goods-to-person workflows, delivered through long-running integration partnerships with KNAPP (Pick-it-Easy Robot, since 2020) and ABB (warehouse robotics, since 2020), as well as deployments with retailers and logistics providers worldwide. In August 2024, Amazon announced a non-exclusive license to Covariant's robotic foundation models and hired its three co-founders along with roughly a quarter of its workforce in a reverse-acquihire arrangement; Covariant continues to operate independently under COO-turned-CEO Ted Stinson and co-founder Tianhao Zhang. The Covariant Brain and RFM-1 are proprietary, deployed on-premise on partner robotics hardware, and the company has no public developer API, SDK, open-source release, or third-party developer program.

providers.name: Flowserve
providers.description: Flowserve moves, controls and protects the flow of materials in the world's most critical industries through pumps, seals, valves, and flow control systems. No public developer APIs have been identified; the company offers digital services such as RedRaven IIoT monitoring through customer engagements rather than an open developer portal.

providers.name: Hexcel
providers.description: Hexcel Corporation (NYSE: HXL) is a global leader in advanced composite materials for the aerospace, defense and space, and industrial markets. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut and operating roughly 18 manufacturing facilities worldwide with about 5,800 employees, Hexcel produces HexTow carbon fiber, HexPly prepregs, HexWeb honeycomb, HexForce reinforcements, HexBond adhesives, HexFlow infusion resins, and HexTool tooling materials supplied into commercial aircraft, military platforms, space launch vehicles, wind energy blades, and industrial structures. Hexcel is a critical materials supplier to Boeing and Airbus and supports more than 100 defense programs; it has no public developer portal, REST APIs, SDKs, or machine-readable product catalog. Customer interaction with technical resources is PDF-based (datasheets, technology manuals, brochures), and the company's GitHub organization (github.com/Hexcel) is registered but empty.

providers.name: Leucine
providers.description: Leucine is an AI-powered software platform for pharmaceutical manufacturing, quality, and laboratory operations, helping drug manufacturers plan, execute, and optimize every batch. The platform spans a Manufacturing Execution System (batch execution, batch intelligence, production logbooks, batch release, shop floor monitor, material management), a Quality Management System (AI Investigator, FDA Tracker, cleaning validation, market complaints, change control, CAPA, supplier quality, audit and deviation management), and a Laboratory Execution System (environmental monitoring, instrument logbooks, QC planning). Leucine also publishes FDA compliance research including 483 analysis and investigator profiles. As of 2026 the company is migrating its web presence from leucinetech.com and leucine.io to leucine.ai. Leucine is an enterprise SaaS vendor and does not publish a public developer API program, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Physicsx
providers.description: PhysicsX is an AI-native engineering software company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in London (Shoreditch) with an office in New York, building a platform that embeds physics AI directly into industrial engineering and manufacturing workflows. The platform unifies simulation, physics AI, data, and engineering applications into a single foundation, pairing fast AI-driven physics inference (Deep Physics Models) with numerical simulation to compress development cycles and expand the design space engineers can explore. It integrates with industry-standard CAE/CAD tooling (ANSYS, CATIA, Siemens NX, OpenFOAM, Siemens Star-CCM+), runs cloud-agnostically across AWS and Azure plus hybrid and on-premises deployments, and serves aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy and renewables. Born out of Formula One, PhysicsX has raised roughly $489M across five rounds from investors including General Catalyst, Atomico, Temasek, NVIDIA, Siemens, and Applied Materials. There is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Reliance, Inc.
providers.description: Reliance, Inc. (NYSE: RS) is the largest metals service center operator in North America, distributing approximately 100,000 metal products across aluminum, brass, alloy, copper, carbon steel, stainless steel, titanium, and specialty metals to over 125,000 customers including fabricators and manufacturers. Operating under more than 75 distinct brands across 300+ locations in the US, Canada, and internationally, Reliance provides value-added processing services including cutting, shearing, sawing, leveling, stamping, and just-in-time delivery for aerospace, automotive, construction, defense, energy, electronics, and semiconductor end markets.

providers.name: Stegra
providers.description: Stegra (formerly H2 Green Steel) is a Stockholm-headquartered industrial company, founded in 2020 and backed by Vargas Holding, building what it describes as Europe's first large-scale near-zero-emission steel plant in Boden, northern Sweden. The 270-hectare Boden site integrates a giga-scale electrolyzer producing green hydrogen from renewable Nordic electricity, a direct-reduction plant making green iron without coking coal, and a downstream steel mill — a combination Stegra says cuts steelmaking emissions by roughly 95 percent versus the blast-furnace route. Its commercial products are green steel, green iron and green hydrogen, sold to automotive, construction and appliance customers. Stegra is a heavy-industry manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it operates no public developer portal, publishes no API documentation, and serves no machine-readable API contract. Its only public engineering surface is the stegraab GitHub organization, which maintains community Terraform providers and a tflint ruleset used for its own internal infrastructure.

providers.name: Verdagy
providers.description: Verdagy is a Moss Landing, California clean-energy hardware company that designs and manufactures dynamic alkaline water electrolysis systems for large-scale green hydrogen production. Its eDynamic platform runs very large-area membrane-based electrochemical cells at high current density with dynamic turndown, so electrolyzers can follow intermittent renewable power, targeting fossil-fuel cost parity for clean hydrogen by 2028 without subsidies. The company operates a 2 MW eDynamic demonstration plant at Moss Landing with more than 21,000 commercial cell hours, plus 500 kW and 100 kW test plants, and opened a DOE-supported gigawatt-scale manufacturing facility of more than 100,000 square feet in Newark, California. Verdagy sells electrolyzer hardware and project capacity to industrial hydrogen buyers — refining, ammonia, methanol, e-fuels and SAF — rather than software; it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: B&L Information Systems
providers.description: B&L Information Systems, LLC is a metalcasting-focused enterprise resource planning (ERP) software company founded more than 50 years ago and headquartered in Bridgman, Michigan. Its flagship product, Odyssey ERP, is a cloud-based ERP purpose-built for foundries, die casters, and investment casters, spanning manufacturing, sales, inventory, quality, finance, and data analytics. B&L pairs the software with implementation, consulting, data-conversion, training, and support services tailored to the metalcasting industry. The company is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. As of this enrichment pass, B&L does not publish a public developer portal, REST API documentation, SDKs, or an OpenAPI definition, so this profile captures company identity and public web properties rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Connected Robotics
providers.description: Connected Robotics Inc. is a Japanese foodtech startup, founded in 2014 by Tetsuya Sawanobori and headquartered in Koganei, Tokyo, that develops specialized robotics and AI systems to automate labor-intensive work across food factories and restaurants. Its product line pairs AI image-processing and robot-control technology with purpose-built machines including the Delibot S plating robot, Delibot X filling robot, AI inspection software, a soft-serve ice-cream robot, and a french-fry cooking robot, targeting labor shortages, productivity, and food safety. The company has raised multiple rounds (including a July 2019 Series A led by Global Brain and a Series B closed in 2023 with strategic investors such as Yaskawa Electric, Hoshizaki, and Mitsubishi HC Capital) and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As a hardware and robotics manufacturer, Connected Robotics publishes no public web API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Dryft
providers.description: Dryft, Inc. is a Palo Alto, California startup building an AI operating system for manufacturing operations. The platform pairs context-aware, agent-based intelligence with mathematical optimization to mimic, optimize, and automate complex human decisions across the shop floor and supply chain. Dryft reads operational data from existing ERPs and inventory systems, identifies issues such as late items or stockouts, and autonomously recommends and executes actions like adjusting order quantities and safety stocks or following up with suppliers. The company frames this as a shift from static Enterprise Resource Planning to Enterprise Resource Automation, freeing planners to focus on strategy over administrative work. Founded in 2024 by CEO Anna-Julia Storch and CTO Leonie Freisinger, Dryft raised a $5M round led by General Catalyst with participation from Neo and Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners. Dryft does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation; this profile captures its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Graphite Innovation and Technologies
providers.description: Graphite Innovation and Technologies Inc, operating as GIT Coatings, is a Canadian materials-science company that develops sustainable, graphene-based marine coatings for commercial ships. Its biocide-free hard foul-release hull and propeller coatings, including XGIT-FORCE, XGIT-VORTEX, and XGIT-PROP, cut fuel consumption, reduce drag, and eliminate leaching to protect the marine environment. The company is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. It is a physical-products manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company-level discovery and coverage.

providers.name: HONESS (Shanghai Hongji Environmental Protection)
providers.description: HONESS (泓济环保 / Shanghai Hongji Environmental Protection, honess.cn) is a Chinese environmental services provider founded in 2006, specializing in industrial wastewater treatment and the broader treatment of the "three wastes" (wastewater, waste gas, and hazardous waste). It offers customized environmental solutions, environmental equipment manufacturing and integration, EPC delivery for energy and chemical full-water systems, fine-chemical waste treatment, process packages for new and upgraded wastewater plants, and technology-enabled ("smart") digital operations and maintenance. The company holds top-grade design and contracting qualifications, has delivered 500+ design/build/operation projects for 300+ clients across China and abroad, and operates manufacturing and R&D bases in Shanghai and Anhui. It is not a developer/API company; the public surface is a WordPress corporate site with no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or OAuth. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Iwarranty
providers.description: iWarranty is a London-based, AI and machine-learning powered warranty management software platform that digitizes the entire warranty lifecycle for manufacturers, retailers, warrantors, and consumers. The platform covers QR-code product registration, automated claims processing and verification, repair and replacement coordination, fraud detection, and real-time product performance analytics, and integrates with existing ERP and CRM systems such as SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle, and NetSuite. iWarranty emphasizes sustainability by reducing paper waste and e-waste through digitized processes. The company is backed by Anthemis and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network enrichment lead.

providers.name: Mach Industries
providers.description: Mach Industries develops and manufactures asymmetric aerospace and defense systems and components at scale, with a product portfolio that includes the Viper vertical-takeoff attack drone, the Glide precision strike munition, the Stratos high-altitude pseudo-satellite, the Pike long-range munition, the Dart counter-drone kinetic interceptor, and energetics testing services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The company is a defense hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer or API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Material Evolution
providers.description: Material Evolution is a UK-based cleantech manufacturer of ultra-low carbon cement for the construction industry. Its MevoCem and MevoXL products use a proprietary "Alkali Fusion" process to transform industrial byproducts into cement feedstocks, achieving a 52.5N strength rating at roughly 144-196 kg CO2e per tonne versus ordinary Portland cement. The company operates compact, automated factories (including its Wrexham facility) and applies AI to material development and feedstock optimization. It is a B2B cement supplier and does not currently publish any public developer-facing API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: MeetFuture Technology
providers.description: MeetFuture Technology (弥费科技) is a Shanghai-based, global-leading supplier of semiconductor Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS) and core components, founded in 2014. It designs and manufactures overhead hoist transport (OHT), stocker/storage, purge, and AMHS control-software solutions for semiconductor wafer fabrication plants, integrating with fab MES systems over SEMI equipment communication standards (E37/HSMS, E30/GEM, E82, E84, E10). MeetFuture holds 300+ intellectual-property items, operates China's largest AMHS cleanroom test center, authored China's first semiconductor OHT standard (T/SICA 006—2024), and won the 2025 SEMI Product Innovation Award. It is a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. MeetFuture is an industrial semiconductor-equipment maker and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained for network identity and discovery.

providers.name: Spider Capital
providers.description: Spider Capital is a seed-stage venture capital firm investing in applied-AI enterprise cloud software that modernizes complex industrial sectors. The firm backs founders across construction, financial services, energy, government, healthcare, insurance, mining, manufacturing, supply chain, and transportation, citing 100+ enterprise cloud investments, a 70%+ seed-to-Series-A graduation rate, and portfolio companies including Mechanical Orchard, Imubit, CoLab, Percepto, Codoxo, Klir, Elara Spatial, and Logiwa. Surfaced as a portfolio company of foundry-group; it publishes no public API or developer surface (venture-capital firm), so this profile carries firm identity rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: 6K
providers.description: 6K Inc is a North Andover, Massachusetts advanced-materials company that produces engineered powders and battery materials with UniMelt, its patented microwave-based production-scale plasma system. Named for the roughly 6,000 K plasma temperature it operates at — the temperature of the surface of the sun — UniMelt uses tightly controlled thermal plasma beams to melt or vaporize precursor feedstock into particles with precise size distribution and crystalline phase, in seconds rather than the days conventional processes require, while cutting energy use and eliminating wastewater. The company operates through two divisions. 6K Additive, with production in Burgettstown, Pennsylvania, makes sustainably sourced metal powders for additive manufacturing — titanium Ti-6Al-4V, nickel superalloys Ni625 and Ni718, stainless SS316L, refractory tungsten, niobium C103, copper C18150 and the HEA1000 refractory alloy — reclaiming CNC scrap and revert metal into premium AM powder. 6K Energy produces domestically sourced lithium-ion battery cathode and solid-state materials including NMC, LFP, LLZO, LMO, LTO and LNMO. Additional applications span semiconductor CMP, specialty ceramics, advanced coatings, lighting and display materials, nano-engineered powders, and federal/defense programs; 6K has received US Department of Defense and Department of Energy awards for domestic critical-materials capacity. 6K is a privately held company whose shares trade on secondary markets. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-31 found no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, developer portal, SDK, MCP server, agent card, or event surface — 6K is a materials manufacturer, not an API provider.

providers.name: ACTIVON Co., Ltd.
providers.description: ACTIVON Co., Ltd. (엑티브온) is a South Korean green-biotechnology materials company founded in 2009 and headquartered in Suwon, Gyeonggi-do, that develops and manufactures cosmetic ingredients and micro-encapsulation technology — skin-safe preservative alternatives, multifunctional actives, emollients, humectants and bio-converted ingredients — alongside functional pigment lines (EnergiON heat-storage, Thermon thermochromic, Photon, Fragron, Memorion, MultiON) sold into textiles, coatings, plastics and cosmetics. It is a specialty-materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract. Its only machine-readable agent surface is the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint and llms.txt served on its corporate site, both probed live by API Evangelist.

providers.name: CMC Materials
providers.description: CMC Materials is a global supplier of consumable materials primarily to the semiconductor industry, including chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) slurries and polishing pads. Acquired by Entegris in 2022, CMC's materials portfolio is now part of the Entegris specialty chemicals and CMP solutions business, serving semiconductor manufacturers through advanced materials and process technologies.

providers.name: I-Pulse
providers.description: I-Pulse Inc. is a U.S.-based industrial technology company founded in 2007 by Robert Friedland and Laurent Frescaline that commercializes High Pulsed Power (HPP) — releasing very short, extremely high-power electrical discharges from small amounts of stored energy to generate magnetic forces, shockwaves, electrical arcs and electric fields. I-Pulse holds 55 patents licensed exclusively to its operating businesses across natural-resource transformation (I-ROX rock comminution, I-Mine, iTerra non-chemical weed control, IPW), the energy transition (G-Pulse pulsed-power geothermal drilling, Blue Spark Geothermal), manufacturing (Bmax electromagnetic metal forming and welding, CSI Technologies high-energy capacitors) and R&D (I-Cube, Typhoon). It operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico and Toulouse, France, with offices in Canada, the UK and Singapore, and signed a $250 million CHIPS R&D award with the U.S. Department of Commerce in 2026 for semiconductor and pulsed-power development. I-Pulse is a hardware and industrial-process company; it publishes no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Juna.ai
providers.description: Juna.ai is a Berlin-based industrial AI company building an Agentic Factory OS — a platform of autonomous AI agents that plan, steer, and continuously improve complex industrial production processes. Its agents ingest live plant data through integrations with existing IT/OT systems (SAP, Siemens, AVEVA, PI Server, Snowflake), model assets and processes into a Factory Graph and Knowledge Graph, detect anomalies, run root-cause analysis, generate reports, and recommend or execute control actions 24/7 with human-in-the-loop oversight and full traceability. Juna targets heavy and process industries including chemicals, cement, pulp & paper, glass, food & beverage, pharma, consumer goods, and industrial manufacturing, focused on maximizing output, quality, energy efficiency, and sustainability. The company is backed by Kleiner Perkins, Norrsken VC, and John Doerr. Juna delivers integration through enterprise engagements and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Riiico
providers.description: RIIICO is a Duesseldorf-based industrial software company building 3D-AI tools that digitalize the factory shop floor. Its platform turns reality scans (point clouds) of existing plants into CAD-ready, pre-classified 3D models, cutting 3D modeling time by up to 80% and accelerating factory retrofit, robot programming, and simulation. RIIICO integrates with NVIDIA Omniverse (OpenUSD) and Siemens Xcelerator, and counts Siemens, Volvo, and Schaeffler among its customers. It won the Siemens Inventors of the Year Award 2024 and is backed by Earlybird, PiLabs, and seed + speed. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Scope
providers.description: Scope (Scope Inspection Ltd, London) is an AI-native inspection platform for the Testing, Inspection, and Certification (TIC) industry and heavy-asset operators. It captures field data through voice, video, and forms (offline-capable), extracts structured data from P&IDs, ASME forms, and inspection drawings, surfaces historical inspection context, and automates report generation in Word, Excel, and PDF. The product pushes results into enterprise CMMS/EAM systems via webhooks and prebuilt connectors, but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface at this time. Backed by Index Ventures and Y Combinator; raised a ~$18-20M round led by Index Ventures in 2026.

providers.name: Verso Corporation
providers.description: Verso Corporation (NYSE: VRS) was a North American producer of coated papers including coated groundwood, coated freesheet, and specialty products used in magazines, catalogs, commercial print, books, and packaging. Headquartered in Miamisburg, Ohio, Verso operated mills in Wisconsin Rapids (Wisconsin), Escanaba (Michigan), Duluth (Minnesota), and historically Luke (Maryland). In March 2022, Swedish pulp and paper group BillerudKorsnäs (now Billerud) completed its acquisition of Verso for $825 million in cash, taking the company private and rebranding it as Billerud Americas Corporation. The Verso standalone brand, ticker, and corporate web presence have been retired; ongoing North American operations, paper grades, and customer relationships now sit inside Billerud's global business.

providers.name: Astra Space
providers.description: Astra is a commercial space company providing dedicated small satellite launch services and flight-proven electric propulsion systems. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Alameda, California, Astra sells two products: Launch Services on Rocket 4 — targeting roughly 600 kg to low Earth orbit at a weekly cadence — and the Astra Spacecraft Engine, a flight-proven Hall-effect electric propulsion system sold in single- and multi-thruster configurations for satellite constellations. Astra became the fastest privately funded U.S. company to reach orbit in 2021 and returned to private ownership in July 2024. Astra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable specification; its buyer-facing surface is a set of launch-services and spacecraft-engine inquiry forms alongside a published Rocket 4 Payload User's Guide and engine data sheet.

providers.name: ElevateBio
providers.description: ElevateBio is an advanced therapies technology company and contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) for cell and gene therapies, headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. Through its BaseCamp cGMP manufacturing and process-development business and its centers of excellence, ElevateBio provides end-to-end capabilities spanning gene editing, viral vectors (AAV and lentivirus), mRNA and RNA therapeutics, induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), analytical and process development, and regulatory CMC support, helping partners advance genetic medicines from concept through commercialization. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund and profiled in the API Evangelist network, ElevateBio operates as a science- and manufacturing-driven organization rather than a public API provider; this profile captures its identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Experic
providers.description: Experic is a specialist powder-handling contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) founded in 2018, headquartered in Cranbury, New Jersey, with an EU clinical supply center in Ireland. The company provides process, analytical and formulation development, clinical and commercial cGMP manufacturing, dry powder inhalation (DPI) and capsule/powder dosing, autoinjector and pen assembly, and clinical trial packaging, labeling, storage and logistics. Experic is a physical-goods manufacturing and clinical supply services business; it publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Pairio
providers.description: Pairio is an AI-powered maintenance assistant for manufacturing and industrial teams, built by Pairio GmbH in Munich, Germany and backed by Y Combinator. Technicians capture voice, photos, and video on the shop floor, and Pairio troubleshoots machine breakdowns, searches technical documentation and maintenance history, identifies spare parts, generates structured maintenance reports, and creates work instructions. It preserves expert knowledge across shifts, sites, and teams to reduce mean time to repair (MTTR) and unplanned downtime, integrating with common ERP, CMMS, EAM, and document-management systems such as SAP, IFS, IBM Maximo, Oracle EAM, Hexagon, SharePoint, and Outlook. Pairio is a consumer-facing mobile/web application and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Firestorm
providers.description: Firestorm (Firestorm Labs, Inc.) is a San Diego based defense technology company founded in 2022 that builds expeditionary manufacturing systems and modular unmanned aerial systems. Its xCELL containerized production unit uses HP Multi Jet Fusion additive manufacturing to 3D print industrial-grade PA-12 nylon composite airframes and spare parts at the tactical edge, feeding modular UAS platforms including the Tempest fixed-wing family and the Squall FPV drone. The company holds a five-year, $100M U.S. Air Force IDIQ and closed an $82M Series B in April 2026 led by Washington Harbour Partners. Firestorm ships hardware, not software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Fortera
providers.description: Fortera is a Silicon Valley materials-technology company advancing zero-CO2 cement. Its ReCarb process economically converts captured CO2 into ReAct green cement that meets regulatory standards and can be blended with or used in place of Ordinary Portland Cement inside existing production infrastructure. Fortera operates its first commercial ReCarb plant in Redding, California, holds 100+ patents, and is backed by Khosla Ventures and Temasek. The company is a climate-tech materials producer rather than a software/API provider; it publishes a public marketing website and an llms.txt but no developer API surface.

providers.name: INDOS
providers.description: INDOS (Garment IO) is an AI-powered manufacturing operations platform built for labor-intensive garment and apparel production facilities. Its cloud-based system unifies Manufacturing Execution (MES), Quality Management (QMS), Maintenance Management (MMS), and Warehouse Management (WMS) into a single real-time view of the factory floor. A shop-floor hardware device captures operator and production-line data, and the platform surfaces operator efficiency, AI anomaly detection, performance scorecards, and end-to-end control from cutting through packing. Founded by Ahmed Nounou and Mahmoud Sabae and backed by 500 Global, it serves garment manufacturers across the Middle East, North Africa, and South Asia. INDOS does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: MKS Instruments
providers.description: MKS Instruments is a global provider of foundational technology solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, electronics and packaging, and specialty industrial markets. Its product portfolio spans vacuum and gas delivery systems, photonics, lasers, optics, motion control, and process control. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified at the corporate level; technical integration is typically handled through product-level documentation, sales engineering, and partner channels.

providers.name: yesmro
providers.description: YESMRO (易买工品), operated by Shanghai Sheti Information Technology Co., Ltd. and founded in April 2016, is a self-operated Chinese B2B e-commerce platform for MRO (maintenance, repair and operations) and factory-automation parts. It carries millions of SKUs across mechanical components, industrial control (PLCs, HMIs, servos, drives), sensors, low-voltage electrical, pneumatics, tools, safety and factory consumables from 800+ brands, targeting the small and medium-sized end factories that make up the long tail of industrial demand. The company runs automated (AGV) warehouses in Shanghai, Hefei and Dongguan and 10+ regional offices, and in 2020 launched an open platform for upstream suppliers. It is backed by Qiming Venture Partners, Matrix Partners China and Sequoia Capital China. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming; no public developer API, open-platform docs, or specification surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Apptronik
providers.description: Apptronik is an Austin, Texas-based humanoid robotics company founded in 2016 as a spinout from the Human Centered Robotics Lab at the University of Texas at Austin. Co-founded by Jeff Cardenas (CEO), Dr. Nick Paine (CTO), and Dr. Luis Sentis (scientific advisor), the company designs and manufactures Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot standing 5'8", weighing 160 lbs, capable of lifting 55 lbs, and running for roughly 4 hours on a swappable battery. Apollo targets warehouse, manufacturing, and logistics applications including trailer unloading, case picking, palletization, machine tending, and workcell delivery. Apptronik has commercial pilot programs and partnerships with Mercedes-Benz (automotive manufacturing logistics), GXO Logistics (multi-phase R&D in U.S. distribution centers), Jabil (supply-chain partner helping scale production and an internal Apollo deployment), and Google DeepMind (Apollo integrates Gemini Robotics vision-language-action models). The company previously built NASA's Valkyrie humanoid and ten-plus other research robots. As of February 2026 Apptronik had raised more than $935M (including a $520M Series A-X extension) at a reported $5B valuation, with investors including B Capital, Google, and Mercedes-Benz. The company sells/leases Apollo to enterprise customers via a direct contact-sales motion and ships a proprietary "point-and-click" control suite for deploying solutions; there is no public developer portal, no published REST/AsyncAPI/gRPC API, no public SDK, no open-source release, and no public GitHub repositories under the `apptronik` org.

providers.name: EcoPlant
providers.description: EcoPlant provides an intelligent air compressor control and monitoring platform for industrial facilities. The Ecoplant 360 solution uses IoT sensors, AI-powered dynamic controls, and predictive analytics to optimize compressed-air systems in real time, preventing downtime, improving reliability, and reducing compressed-air energy costs by up to 50 percent. It installs in under a week with no installation fees and is compatible with most compressor brands and existing plant technology.

providers.name: Eastman Chemical
providers.description: Driven by more than 100 years of continuous innovation, Eastman is a global Fortune 500 specialty materials company that produces a broad range of advanced materials, chemicals, and fibers used in everyday products. Eastman operates a customer-facing Customer Center for orders, documents, and Safety Data Sheets, but no public developer portal or REST API has been documented.

providers.name: Amca
providers.description: Amca (Advanced Manufacturing Company of America) is an El Segundo, California aerospace and defense manufacturer rebuilding America's industrial base by acquiring specialized component suppliers and expanding competition and capacity for critical parts — actuators, switches, hydraulics, pressure sensors, power electronics, and flight-control electronics. Founded in 2024 by Eli Giovanetti and Jai Malik, Amca combines design, testing, and production into a single RAPID platform across a network of AS9100D-certified factories (Electro-Mech Components, Electrocube, Aerospace Control Products, Payne Magnetics, Cal-Draulics, BC Power Systems), and serves nearly every major aerospace and defense prime and Tier 1 supplier — Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Airbus, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, Textron, BAE Systems, and the Defense Logistics Agency. It is a hardware manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Bunge
providers.description: Bunge Global SA is a multinational agribusiness and food company connecting farmers to consumers by sourcing, processing, and supplying oilseed and grain products. Operates across grain origination, oilseed processing, refined and specialty oils, milling, sugarcane and biofuel production, and fertilizer sales. In 2025 Bunge completed its merger with Viterra to create a major global agricultural trading and processing platform.

providers.name: Cameron International
providers.description: Cameron International (formerly Cooper Cameron Corporation) was a leading provider of flow equipment products, systems, and services to the worldwide oil, gas, and process industries. In 2016 the business was acquired by Schlumberger (now SLB) and its pressure-control, drilling, subsea, valves, measurement, and compression product lines were integrated into SLB's digital oilfield portfolio. Cameron-branded capabilities are now delivered and integrated through the SLB DELFI digital platform and its developer APIs rather than through a standalone Cameron developer program.

providers.name: Crown Holdings
providers.description: Crown Holdings, Inc. is a global leader in the design, manufacture, and sale of rigid packaging products for consumer goods, including metal beverage cans and ends, food cans, aerosol cans, specialty closures and promotional tins, as well as transit and protective packaging products for industrial markets. The company operates in more than 40 countries and supports customers with design, decoration, reprographics, compound development, pilot facilities, and seaming training services. Crown Holdings does not publish a public developer API program; technical collaboration with customers happens through B2B and EDI channels.

providers.name: Varda Space Industries
providers.description: Varda Space Industries is an American space manufacturing company founded in 2021 and headquartered in El Segundo, California. Varda designs, builds and flies the W-Series, a free-flying orbital production satellite paired with a hypersonic reentry capsule, so that materials can be processed in microgravity and returned to Earth. The company sells three lines of service: biopharmaceutical processing (small-molecule crystallization that gravity disrupts on Earth), a government hypersonic flight testbed that uses the capsule's Mach 25 reentry as a test article carrier, and general microgravity research flights. Varda is a hardware and manufacturing-services business rather than a software vendor: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification, and customer-facing technical interfaces are documented in a downloadable Payload User Guide PDF.

providers.name: CarbonChain
providers.description: CarbonChain is a London- and New York-based carbon accounting platform founded in 2019 that is purpose-built for the highest-emitting, hardest-to- track commodity supply chains — metals and mining, energy, manufacturing, and agriculture. Its AI-assisted platform builds asset- and transaction- level emissions pictures using activity-based emission factors, and packages those calculations into modules for supply-chain emissions, corporate carbon footprints (Scope 1, 2, 3), product carbon footprints, scenario analysis, and regulatory compliance. The flagship CarbonChain Comply release ships a Carbon Reporting Hub aligned with EU CSRD, UK SECR, US SEC, and CDP, along with EU/UK CBAM declaration validation, automated CBAM XML generation, and a Supplier Engagement Module for collecting and validating supplier emissions data. CarbonChain Connect links producers and importers through shared installation-level CBAM infrastructure. The company is a CDP Accredited Provider (2024), is ISO 27001 certified, and is backed by Y Combinator, Union Square Ventures, Voyager VC, and Aera VC, with $10M Series A funding (2023). CarbonChain serves manufacturers, commodity traders, banks, and procurement teams, and offers system-to-system API integration for delivering activity data in and pulling gold-standard emissions calculations out — but it does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source client library. API access is offered as part of customer integration projects rather than as a self-serve developer surface.

providers.name: Celanese
providers.description: Celanese Corporation is a global chemical and specialty materials company that produces high-performance engineered polymers and acetyl products used across automotive, medical, consumer, and industrial applications. Celanese has no publicly documented developer API; digital engagement is delivered through the Chemille digital materials assistant for product search and selection, and a Cognite Data Fusion based manufacturing data platform for internal operations.

providers.name: Heineken
providers.description: A Dutch multinational brewing company and one of the world's largest beer producers. Operates over 165 breweries across 70 countries producing iconic brands including Heineken, Amstel, Tecate, and Dos Equis. Maintains an internal HEIWAY API portal (api-portal.production.az.heiway.com) used for partner, distributor, and on-trade B2B integrations; access is gated and not openly published.

providers.name: Path Robotics
providers.description: Path Robotics is a Columbus, Ohio autonomous welding robotics company founded in 2018 by brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (CEO and CTO) out of Case Western Reserve University. The company builds AI-powered intelligent welding cells that automate metal fabrication for defense shipyards, utility and energy infrastructure, data centers, and heavy industry. Its core technology is Obsidian, a physical-AI reinforcement-learning agent trained inside Path's proprietary Weld World Model on tens of millions of welded inches; Obsidian runs at the edge of each cell and makes real-time, seam-by-seam welding decisions using a sensor stack of two cameras plus four lasers that deliver sub-millimeter 360-degree awareness around the torch. Path markets the cells with a CapEx-free consumption model and reports 97%+ first-pass yield, 4x productivity, and 30% lower welding costs across customers including HII (America's largest military shipbuilder), Saronic, LAD Services, Tycrop, Mine Rite Technologies, and Millerbernd. In April 2026 Path announced Rove, a mobile welding system mounted on a quadruped platform, extending its addressable geometry beyond fixed-cell applications. The company has raised approximately $271M across Seed through Series D from Drive Capital, Matter Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Addition, and Yamaha Motor Ventures, with the most recent $100M Series D closing in October 2024. Path Robotics has no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; its GitHub organization contains roughly 50 repositories that are almost entirely upstream open-source forks (ROS, protobuf, abseil, ceres-solver, pytorch3d, etc.) used as internal build dependencies rather than published developer artifacts. Revenue is earned through welding-cell deployments, services, and the consumable weld-output model — not API monetization.

providers.name: ShelterLogic Group
providers.description: ShelterLogic Group is the world leader in shade, shelter, storage, and outdoor lifestyle products with over 70 years of industry experience. Launched in 1991, ShelterLogic develops tough, affordable shelter solutions for everyday consumers and commercial customers. The company operates three manufacturing facilities in the US and China and maintains worldwide distribution. The ShelterLogic brand portfolio includes ShelterLogic, SOJAG, Arrow Storage Products, Quik Shade, CAMP&GO, RIO Beach, and licensed brands including Tommy Bahama, Margaritaville, Life is Good, and Scotts Miracle-Gro. As a B2C manufacturer and retailer, ShelterLogic does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Silgan Holdings
providers.description: Silgan Holdings Inc. is a leading global sustainable packaging provider for consumer goods products. The company partners with customers to deliver essential products to the world in efficient, sustainable, and cost-effective packaging formats. Silgan operates through three primary business segments: Dispensing and Specialty Closures, Metal Containers, and Custom Containers. With 123 manufacturing facilities on four continents, over 17,200 employees, and approximately $6 billion in annual sales, Silgan serves the food, beverage, healthcare, home and garden, personal care, fragrance, and beauty end markets.

providers.name: Thor Industries
providers.description: Thor Industries is the world's largest manufacturer of recreational vehicles, owning subsidiary brands including Airstream, Jayco, Heartland RV, Keystone RV, and others. Thor Industries operates primarily as a manufacturing company and does not publish a public developer API. Dealer integrations and connected vehicle features are managed through subsidiary brands and OEM partnerships.

providers.name: AAK
providers.description: AAK AB is a Swedish producer of value-adding plant-based oils and fats, headquartered in Malmö and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ticker AAK) in the Food & Beverage large-cap segment. It was formed in 2005 through the merger of Denmark's Aarhus United and Sweden's Karlshamns AB, and describes more than 150 years of combined experience in specialty vegetable oils. The company employs roughly 4,000 people across 19 production facilities, 25 regional sales offices and 16 Customer Innovation Centers, and works through a co-development model with customers in chocolate and confectionery, bakery, dairy and ice cream, plant-based foods, special nutrition, foodservice and retail, personal care, animal nutrition, candles and technical products such as fatty acids and glycerine. Its product is a physical industrial ingredient, not software: no developer program, public API, SDK, developer portal, machine-readable contract or GitHub organization could be found, and no api/developer/docs/portal hostname resolves under aak.com.

providers.name: Advance Composite
providers.description: Advance Composite Corporation (アドバンスコンポジット株式会社) is a Japanese advanced-materials manufacturer founded on 22 July 2015 and headquartered at 2259-9 Oobuchi, Fuji City, Shizuoka Prefecture, with a Tokyo branch in Otemachi, Chiyoda-ku. The company develops, manufactures and sells metal matrix composite (MMC) materials and joined products using a proprietary squeeze-casting / molten-metal forging process that impregnates reinforcement materials such as graphite, alumina and other ceramics with molten aluminium under high pressure, producing parts with few internal voids. Its published material families include the ACM-H series (New ACM-H1/H2/H3 aluminium-graphite composites), AC-Alox (aluminium/alumina) and AC-Albolon, marketed on high thermal conductivity, low thermal expansion, low density and high stiffness for semiconductor manufacturing equipment, data centres, air conditioning, medical devices, mobility and rail. It is ISO 9001:2015 certified (Intertek registration 15556, UKAS accredited, first issued 2023-11-08), won the IVS2025 LAUNCHPAD, and raised a Series B from Kyoto iCAP in 2026. Advance Composite is a physical-materials manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Aerofugia
providers.description: Aerofugia (沃飞长空, Sichuan Aerofugia Technology Development Co., Ltd.) is a Chengdu-based advanced air mobility company founded in 2020 under Zhejiang Geely Holding Group's Geely Technology Group, focused on the research, certification and commercial operation of low-altitude passenger aircraft. Its flagship product is the AE200 series, a six-seat all-electric piloted eVTOL with a roughly 200 km range aimed at intercity air mobility, low-altitude tourism and emergency medical transport; the AE200 was the first piloted eVTOL type certificate application accepted by the Civil Aviation Administration of China, has completed full tilt-transition flight testing, and the company holds a CCAR-135 air operator certificate. As of this profile Aerofugia publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract: it is an aircraft manufacturer and future air-mobility operator, not a platform vendor.

providers.name: Brimstone
providers.description: Brimstone is a materials technology company decarbonizing heavy industry through a single-rock co-production process it calls the Rock Refinery. From ordinary calcium silicate rock it extracts multiple high-value materials at once - carbon-negative Portland cement and supplementary cementitious materials, alumina and aluminum, magnesium, titanium, iron/steel feedstock and critical minerals - aiming to use 100% of the feed rock and eliminate tailings while cutting process emissions. The company uses commercially available equipment for a low-cost, market-ready approach, and has secured commitments including Amazon as a buyer of low-carbon cement from its first commercial plant. Brimstone is a private heavy-industry / climate-tech company backed by DCVC and Fifth Wall; it operates no public developer API.

providers.name: Cambium
providers.description: Cambium is an advanced materials company (Cambium Biomaterials, El Segundo, California, founded 2019) that molecularly re-engineers polymers from first principles, pairing AI-driven molecular design with chemistry, materials science, biology, and agile domestic manufacturing to develop and scale next-generation materials roughly 10x faster than traditional methods. Product lines span thermal protection systems, high-temperature structural polymers, and laser/directed-energy protection, serving aerospace, space, defense, motorsport, automotive, marine, and industrial customers. Its SHD Advanced Composites business runs rapid-response prepreg manufacturing across the US, UK, and EU. Backed by 8VC. Cambium publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures corporate identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: Cliffs Natural Resources
providers.description: Cliffs Natural Resources is the legacy corporate name for what is now Cleveland-Cliffs Inc., a major mining and natural resources company that produces iron ore pellets primarily for steelmaking customers in North America. The company was renamed Cleveland-Cliffs in 2017 and the canonical profile lives at the cleveland-cliffs repo. Cliffs Natural Resources / Cleveland-Cliffs does not publish a public developer portal or general-purpose REST API surface.

providers.name: Cubenergy
providers.description: Cubenergy (ShenZhen Cubenergy Co., Ltd. / 库博能源) is a BloombergNEF Tier 1 manufacturer of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and utility-scale deployments. The company integrates self-developed Battery Systems, BMS, and EMS with grid, PV, wind, and diesel generation into standardized, all-in-one, transportable, EPC-free energy storage products (FlexCombo, PowerCombo E5, FlexCombo D2, FlexCube C1). Its products are certified to UL9540, UL9540A, and NFPA855, and it offers an O&M platform plus bankability (DNV certified, AIG insured) for funded and insured projects. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Cubenergy publishes a corporate marketing site with no public developer/API program at this time.

providers.name: Diamond Foundry
providers.description: Diamond Foundry is a deep-tech materials company that manufactures semiconductor-grade single-crystal diamond wafers and diamond transistors to overcome the thermal limits of silicon in AI chips, datacenters, and electric vehicles. The company operates its own foundries and has built a full technology stack for producing diamond at scale as a sustainable substrate for high-performance and power electronics. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a planetary-health portfolio company of Obvious Ventures; it publishes no public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Elementary
providers.description: Elementary is an AI-powered machine-vision inspection company for manufacturing, founded in 2017 in South Pasadena, California (originally Elementary Robotics). Its VisionStream self-training edge AI detects production defects in seconds without rules, labeling, or tuning, while the QualityOS cloud platform delivers traceability, analytics, and MES/ERP integration across production lines. Elementary inspects over one billion parts annually for Fortune 500 manufacturers across food & beverage, automotive, consumer packaged goods, electronics, and life sciences, and is backed by Rockwell Automation, Tiger Global, Toyota Ventures, Threshold Ventures, Fika Ventures, and Idealab. The company exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: EVERSTEEL
providers.description: EVERSTEEL is a University of Tokyo-originated startup building AI image-recognition systems that automate the inspection and grading of steel (iron) scrap for steelmakers. Its flagship product, Tetsu-Navi Inspection AI (鉄ナビ検収AI), uses high-resolution cameras and computer-vision models to grade incoming scrap, detect impurities and hazardous materials, and standardize what was previously a manual, expert-dependent process — advancing steel recycling and reducing CO2 emissions from steel production. The company works with major Japanese steel producers including JFE Steel and Kyoei Steel, and is backed by DCM Ventures, Mitsui & Co., Coreline, and the University of Tokyo.

providers.name: Hertha Metals
providers.description: Hertha Metals is a hard-technology steel production company based in Conroe, Texas, working to decarbonize and modernize primary steelmaking after centuries of coke-based blast-furnace iron and steel production. Founded by Laureen Meroueh, the company has developed proprietary pyrometallurgical HERS and Flex-HERS technology that produces steel from flexible feedstocks in a single reactor, and has raised roughly $17M toward a commercial steel plant. Hertha Metals is an industrial / climate-tech manufacturer with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Khosla Ventures portfolio company profile.

providers.name: INURU
providers.description: INURU (Inuru GmbH) is a Berlin-based printed-electronics company that manufactures ultra-thin, flexible printed OLED lighting for smart packaging, labels, apparel, and medical products. Its core product, the Elf (Embeddable Luminous Film), combines an inkjet-printed OLED, a power source, and a microchip into a paper-thin, waterproof film that can glow in any shape and respond to touch, motion, or sound. Founded in 2016, Inuru operates the automated "Dragon Factory" OLED production line in Wildau and works with brands such as Coca-Cola and Marvel on interactive, sustainable smart-packaging and medication-adherence labels. This is a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network; Inuru is a hardware and smart-packaging manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: iTAC Software
providers.description: iTAC Software AG is an independent company of the Duerr Group and a leading provider of Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for discrete manufacturing. Its iTAC.MOM.Suite delivers production control, end-to-end traceability, quality management, and AI-supported analytics that help automotive, electronics, and medical-technology manufacturers implement Industry 4.0 and smart-factory operations. iTAC does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; system integration is delivered through the MOM platform's IoT and connectivity layers as part of a project engagement.

providers.name: MicroBenefits
providers.description: MicroBenefits is a workforce-engagement and HR technology company, backed by 500 Global, that created CompanyIQ — a scalable mobile platform for improving engagement, learning, and communication for factory and manufacturing workers, particularly across Asia. CompanyIQ bundles Worker Voice (employee feedback and dialogue), Digital Learning (safety, rights, and professional-development training), an Employee Portal (wage, hours, and benefits transparency), and Business Intelligence workforce analytics, alongside professional and learning services. The company operates a marketing and support presence but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or specification surface at this time.

providers.name: Oshkosh
providers.description: Oshkosh Corporation is a Fortune 500 industrial company that designs and builds purpose-built vehicles and vehicle bodies, including access equipment, defense vehicles, fire and emergency apparatus, refuse collection vehicles, and concrete mixers.

providers.name: Pretred
providers.description: Pretred is a Techstars-backed manufacturer of sustainable rubber safety barriers made from recycled waste tires, serving the infrastructure, traffic control, and construction sectors with a circular-economy model. Its product line spans the Standard Rubber Barrier, TL-2 and TL-3 crash-tested barriers, a Load-Rated Barrier rated for heavy machinery, and Paceline bike-lane barriers, each engineered for energy absorption, durability, and modularity. Every Pretred facility can divert over 100 million pounds of waste tires from landfills or incineration annually. As a physical-goods manufacturer, Pretred publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface; this profile captures the company identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: ProLogium Technology
providers.description: ProLogium Technology Co., Ltd. is a Taiwanese energy-innovation company founded in 2006 that develops and manufactures next-generation solid-state lithium ceramic batteries built around a 100% ceramic separator. It commercialized its first solid-state cells in 2013, opened the world's first giga-level solid-state lithium ceramic battery plant in Taoyuan, Taiwan in 2024, and operates a European R&D center at Paris-Saclay with a planned gigafactory in Dunkirk, France. Its product lines span FLCB, PLCB and LLCB cells plus battery modules and packs, targeting electric vehicles, energy storage systems, robotics, and consumer and industrial applications. ProLogium is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Verkor
providers.description: Verkor is a French cleantech manufacturer founded in 2020 to fast-track low-carbon lithium-ion battery production in Europe. Operating a "digital by design" industrial model, Verkor produces high-performance battery cells and modules for electric mobility and stationary energy storage, scaling through its Dunkerque Gigafactory toward 16 GWh of annual cell capacity to serve the European market. Verkor is a physical-products/industrial company and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and public web surface within the API Evangelist network. Backed by EQT Ventures.

providers.name: Aurorin CAD
providers.description: Aurorin CAD is a San Francisco company building a modern mechanical CAD application for engineers and hardware teams, founded in 2026 by Michael Baron and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Rather than layering on top of the geometry kernels that underpin incumbent tools such as SolidWorks, NX, Creo, CATIA, Fusion 360 and Onshape, Aurorin has written its own parametric, B-Rep driven CAD kernel designed to exploit modern multi-core CPUs and GPUs and to be AI-native from the foundation rather than as a bolted-on assistant. The product ships as a native desktop application for macOS and Windows, pairing conventional direct and parametric editing with an integrated AI agent driven through a chat interface, with the stated goal of collapsing modeling work that traditionally takes twenty minutes into seconds and avoiding the slow rebuilds and cascading feature breakage common to older parametric systems. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or API documentation; its public surface is a marketing site, a blog, an about/contact page, and careers listings.

providers.name: Kaizntree Inc.
providers.description: Kaizntree is a New York-based operations platform for growth-stage consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands, giving multi-channel manufacturers and sellers a single system to run purchasing, inventory, sales, fulfillment, production, and lot-level traceability. Its two products are Kaizntree OS, a cloud ERP that centralizes stock across raw materials, intermediate goods, packaging, finished and bundled products with COGS, margin, multi-location, batch/expiry and audit-ready records, and JP, an ERP-agnostic AI operations assistant that automates high-volume workflows such as purchase-order processing, reporting, data synchronization, and OTIF tracking. Kaizntree integrates with sales channels (including Shopify), accounting, WMS, and fulfillment platforms. Backed by 500 Global (seed, 2022), it operates on usage-based pricing. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; Kaizntree publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Addionics
providers.description: Addionics is a Smart Metals manufacturer headquartered in London, United Kingdom, with operations in Israel, Korea and the USA, building Smart 3D Porous Current Collectors that replace the flat copper and aluminium foils inside a battery cell with a porous, ion-permeable metal architecture. The technology is chemistry-agnostic and drop-in, produced roll-to-roll on existing coating lines, and is sold into robotics, defence, space and EV programmes. Addionics is a hardware and materials company: it operates no developer program and publishes no API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable API contract. It does run a deliberate agent-readable content surface on its own domain — a served /llms.txt digest, a published /agents.md agent guide, a markdown twin of every page under Accept: text/markdown, a complete /sitemap.xml and an RSS blog feed — all captured in this profile.

providers.name: Aeon Industrial
providers.description: Aeon Industrial is an American defense technology company, founded in 2023 and headquartered in the Austin, Texas area, that designs and manufactures affordable precision tactical weapon systems. Its two named products are ODIN, an autonomous precision targeting software package that observes, detects, interrogates and neutralizes threats and is advertised as an open architecture installable on third-party hardware, and Zeus, a modular software-defined tactical missile system powered by ODIN. The company is vertically integrated, building in-house from commercially available American-made components, and sells to U.S. and allied defense customers. Aeon publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification; its only public machine-readable documents are the OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 discovery files served by its own WorkOS AuthKit identity host for its login-gated partner portal.

providers.name: Convergent Dental
providers.description: Convergent Dental, Inc. is a privately held dental equipment and technology manufacturer headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, best known for Solea, a 9.3 micron CO2 all-tissue dental laser cleared by the FDA for hard tissue, soft tissue and osseous indications. The Solea platform is marketed for anesthesia-free, blood-free and suture-free restorative, soft tissue, pediatric, implant and cosmetic procedures, and has been extended with Solea Perioguide for minimally invasive periodontal therapy, Solea Sleep and Solea Protect. The company sells and services through its own commercial organization and a distribution partnership with Patterson Dental, and supports clinicians with training and education, clinical studies, case studies and the annual Solea Summit. Convergent Dental publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable API contract or agent surface as of this profiling pass.

providers.name: Donkey
providers.description: Donkey is an AI-native trading company (Y Combinator, Summer 2026) that buys directly from Chinese factories and sells delivered duty-paid to US importers. Donkey mines public US customs records to identify the factory that actually makes a product, returns a landed DDP quote within 72 hours, runs its own on-the-floor quality inspections before the factory is paid, clears customs, moves the money, and offers credit-insured net-45 terms to qualified buyers. Founded by Benjamin Martindale (CEO) and Minghao Tan (CTO), the company runs small teams in San Francisco and China. Donkey publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform today; this profile tracks its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Jimmy
providers.description: Jimmy (Jimmy Energy SAS) is a French nuclear-technology company, founded in 2020 as a spin-off from the CEA, that designs, builds and operates small modular high-temperature reactors it calls thermal generators — helium-cooled HTR units the company describes as bus-sized — to deliver carbon-free process heat directly to industrial sites under secured 20-year supply-and-price contracts. Jimmy is headquartered in Paris with an industrial platform at Le Creusot in Burgundy, targets food, paper, sugar and chemicals producers that currently burn natural gas for process heat, and filed the first SMR creation-authorization request in France for a generator at the Cristanol site in Bazancourt. Jimmy sells heat, not software: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification, and this profile records that measured absence rather than assuming it.

providers.name: Lucid Motors
providers.description: Lucid Motors is the consumer-vehicle brand of Lucid Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: LCID), a Newark, California–headquartered American luxury electric vehicle manufacturer. The company designs and manufactures high-performance battery-electric sedans and SUVs, with its flagship Lucid Air (Pure, Touring, Grand Touring, and Sapphire trims) and the Lucid Gravity SUV (Touring and Grand Touring), assembled at its AMP-1 factory in Casa Grande, Arizona. Lucid develops its own electric powertrain, battery, and software stack — including the Lucid UX in-vehicle experience, the Lucid mobile app, Lucid Assistant, and over-the-air updates — and operates a vertically integrated direct-to-consumer sales, financing, leasing, and service model across North America, Europe, and the Middle East, supported by a growing network of Lucid Studios, Service Centers, and DC fast charging partnerships. Lucid is majority-owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF). Beyond consumer vehicles, Lucid licenses its powertrain and battery technology to other OEMs (notably Aston Martin) and supplies battery systems through its Lucid energy storage initiatives. Lucid Motors does not publish a public developer API portal, SDK, or OpenAPI specification; the Lucid mobile app and vehicle telematics are powered by private backend services that are not documented for third-party use.

providers.name: Lyten
providers.description: Lyten is a San Jose, California advanced-materials company founded in 2015 that invented and commercializes Lyten 3D Graphene, a tunable three-dimensional carbon supermaterial produced by converting methane into nanostructured carbon while co-producing hydrogen. Lyten applies that materials platform across four product lines: lithium-sulfur battery cells and battery systems that contain no cobalt, nickel or manganese and target roughly 40% weight savings versus lithium-ion; 3D graphene reinforced 3D printer filament; concrete admixture and structural adhesives; and chemical/environmental sensors, including the Lyten Atmos continuous methane-intelligence platform that pairs solar-powered LTE field sensors with cloud analytics and dashboards for landfill and oil-and-gas emissions monitoring. The company has raised over $600 million from investors including Stellantis, FedEx and Honeywell, operates a 145,000 sq ft pilot manufacturing facility in the Alviso district of North San Jose, acquired Cuberg's San Leandro battery assets in 2024, and in 2025 acquired Northvolt battery manufacturing assets in Poland and Sweden, establishing a European headquarters in Gdansk, Poland. Lyten is a private company; its shares trade on secondary markets such as Forge Global. It publishes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal.

providers.name: Moog
providers.description: Moog Inc. is a worldwide designer, manufacturer, and integrator of precision motion and fluid control products and solutions for aerospace, defense, industrial, and medical applications. Product divisions include actuation, motion systems, motors, propulsion, valves, aerospace components, and defense systems. Moog does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: United Solar
providers.description: United Solar (United Solar Polysilicon FZC SPC) is a clean-technology company producing ultra-high-purity polysilicon for the photovoltaic industry from one of the world's most advanced manufacturing facilities in Oman's Sohar Free Zone, with an annual capacity of 100,000 metric tons supporting roughly 40 GW of solar module production. Backed by IDG Capital and the IFC, the company completed a $1.6 billion capital raise in 2026 and is the largest polysilicon producer of its kind outside China. United Solar is an industrial manufacturer and does not publish a developer portal or public APIs.

providers.name: Varda
providers.description: Varda Space Industries is a microgravity-enabled life sciences company that processes materials in orbit and returns them to Earth. Its in-house W-Series spacecraft are free-flying orbital production satellites with reentry capability, used for in-orbit pharmaceutical crystallization for biopharma partners and as a hypersonic reentry testbed for government flight testing. Backed by Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, and Lux Capital, Varda publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Genomatica
providers.description: Genomatica (which markets itself as Geno) is a San Diego, California biotechnology and sustainable materials company founded in 1998 that engineers microbes and fermentation processes to make widely used chemical building blocks from plants instead of fossil fuels. Its commercialized process technology covers Geno BDO (bio-based 1,4-butanediol, licensed to partners including BASF and Novamont), Brontide butylene glycol for personal care, Avela (R)-1,3-butanediol, plant-based nylon-6 intermediates developed with lululemon and manufacturing partners such as Hyosung and Sojitz, plus palm-oil alternatives and fragrance building blocks. Genomatica licenses its process technology to chemical producers rather than operating a software platform; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable specification, or agent-facing discovery surface.

providers.name: Jeh Aerospace
providers.description: Jeh Aerospace is a precision aerospace manufacturing company building "future factories" across the US-India corridor to supply aerostructures and aero-engine components for the commercial aerospace supply chain. From certified facilities in India spanning more than 160,000 square feet, Jeh delivers machining, sheet metal, tubes and pipes, surface treatment, structural assembly, and engineering services on time and at scale. The company is fully compliant with AS9100, ISO 9001, OEM requirements, and export regulations, and weaves a digital thread across its supplier networks for radical transparency. Jeh operates from both the US and India and is backed by General Catalyst and IndiGo Ventures.

providers.name: Amyris
providers.description: Amyris, Inc. is a synthetic-biology and precision-fermentation company that engineers microbes to convert plant-derived sugars into high-performance renewable molecules — including farnesene, squalene, squalane, and bisabolol — at industrial scale.
